title: Decide the doctor exit-code contract
description:
evalctl's `doctor` exits 0 even when a component is unhealthy. Sibling tool
spoolctl exits 3 in the same situation and reports readiness as `data.ready`.
evalctl's behavior is pinned by a test, so it is deliberate, but the two tools
in the same family disagree on what a health check's exit code means -- and
callers that script both will get it wrong for one of them.

This is not blocked by the failure_reason adoption work or by the conformance
sweep, and neither changes it. It needs its own decision.
acceptance_criteria:
- A decision is recorded: evalctl either keeps exit 0 with an unhealthy
  component, or adopts a nonzero exit, with the reasoning stated.
- If the behavior changes, the pinning test and any documented exit-code table
  are updated together.
- The decision states whether `data.ready` is adopted as the machine-readable
  readiness signal.
notes:
Superseded in scope by `evalctl-exit-code-contract-yxb`, filed from the
v0.4.3 conformance sweep and linked here as `related`.

That bead covers the same question from two more angles and they should be
decided as one, because deciding them apart risks incompatible answers about a
single published dictionary:

- F2. `run --fail-on-fail` exits 6 with `ok: true`, an empty `errors` list
  and nothing on stderr. An agent branching on `ok` and an agent branching on
  the exit code read the same envelope and reach opposite conclusions.
- F22. Exit 2 is published as 'safety block'. Zero of the 33 registered error
  codes map to it and zero of the fifteen verbs declare it, so nothing in the
  tool can emit it.

This bead stays open because the doctor half is a genuine judgement call about
what a diagnostic verb's exit code should mean, and that is a decision to make
deliberately rather than a defect to fix. Either resolve it inside
`evalctl-exit-code-contract-yxb` and close this one into it, or answer it here
first and let that bead implement the result.
close_reason:
Decision recorded (status quo ratified); no code change. Folds into the closed
evalctl-exit-code-contract-yxb.

Decision: doctor keeps exit 0 when a component is unhealthy. A diagnostic verb
reports health in its payload, not through its exit status; the exit code answers
only "could doctor run at all" (0 ran, 1 bad invocation). This is already pinned
by test_doctor_exit_code_is_zero_even_with_an_unhealthy_component and published
as doctor exit_codes [0,1].

Readiness signal: evalctl does NOT adopt spoolctl's data.ready. The machine-
readable signal is the existing envelope field operation_outcome.kind
(healthy | degraded | unhealthy) plus health_kind (all-clear | attention-needed).
The two sibling tools deliberately differ here: spoolctl couples readiness to a
nonzero exit, evalctl keeps a diagnostic's exit clean and puts the verdict in the
envelope. A caller scripting both branches on each tool's documented contract,
not on a shared exit convention.

Since behavior is unchanged, no pinning test or exit-code table needed updating.
The exit-2/exit-6 half of the shared question shipped in 0.4.4 under yxb.

title: Canceled spoolctl job is misdiagnosed as an incompatible spoolctl
description:
A spoolctl job canceled before it runs reports `state: canceled`,
`attempts: []`, `last_failure_reason: null`. Against that payload,
`latest_terminal_attempt` (`evalctl/runner.py:257`) raises
`E_SPOOLCTL_INCOMPATIBLE` with the message "spoolctl show did not include
attempts" -- blaming tool compatibility for an ordinary queue outcome.

Not reachable through evalctl's own flow today: evalctl never cancels, and it
drains synchronously. Reachable by an external `spoolctl cancel` against the
run's `.spoolctl.db`.

Reproduction: queue a job, run `spoolctl cancel` against it before the worker
picks it up, then `spoolctl show --json` -- the job carries an empty `attempts`
list. Verified against real spoolctl 0.4.11.

Deliberately not fixed alongside the failure_reason adoption work: the
resolution likely needs a decision on the `canceled` case status, which exists
in `TERMINAL_CASE_STATUSES` (`evalctl/run_state.py:16`) with nothing producing
it. Giving it a producer is a contract decision, not a passenger on an
unrelated batch.
acceptance_criteria:
A canceled job with no attempts must not be reported as spoolctl
incompatibility.
close_reason: Fixed in 33c6521. latest_terminal_attempt returned E_SPOOLCTL_INCOMPATIBLE for a job canceled before a worker ran it, because such a job reports an empty attempts list and that was not distinguished from a missing attempts key. It now returns None for a present-but-empty list; the queued loop synthesizes a spawn_failed result (runner_result_for_unrun_job), which normalizes to E_RUNNER_FAILED on that case while the run completes. A missing or non-list attempts key still raises E_SPOOLCTL_INCOMPATIBLE. Deliberately does not give the 'canceled' case status a producer -- that stays a separate contract decision. Coverage: FAKE_SPOOLCTL_DROP_ATTEMPTS knob for the end-to-end run, direct unit tests over latest_terminal_attempt and runner_result_for_unrun_job, and a real-spoolctl test that queues a job, cancels it pre-execution, and feeds the real show payload through latest_terminal_attempt. The end-to-end test was verified to fail against the pre-fix read with the exact envelope reported here.

title: Implement runner execution contract
description: The runner is the agent-under-test invocation, and v0.1 must execute it honestly as arbitrary local code while bounding reproducibility and artifact leakage.
design:
Support `runner.argv` with `shell:false` as the default and `runner.command` with `shell:true` as an explicit escape hatch. Exactly one form is valid for the selected mode. Default `cwd` to the per-case workspace. Inherit only `env_allowlist` variables and always inject `EVALCTL_CASE_FILE`, `EVALCTL_WORKSPACE`, `EVALCTL_OUTPUT_FILE`, `EVALCTL_TASK_FILE`, and `EVALCTL_DIFF_FILE` when present.

Close stdin by default, with `runner.stdin:"task"` to pipe task text. Apply `timeout_seconds`, kill the process group on timeout, capture stdout/stderr/output up to `max_output_bytes`, and apply `redact_env_values` and `redact_patterns` before writing artifacts.
acceptance_criteria:
- `shell:false` executes argv without implicit shell joining; `$EVALCTL_*` substitution is performed only by evalctl.
- `shell:true` executes the explicit command through `sh -c` and is documented as the less-safe escape hatch.
- Runner spawn failures and timeouts mark the case `error`; ordinary nonzero process exits are captured and scored rather than treated as tool errors.
- Every `run` emits `W_UNSANDBOXED_RUNNER` in the JSON envelope and prints the warning to stderr when appropriate unless the suite explicitly acknowledges it.
- Captured stdout, stderr, and output are truncated and redacted before persistence, with booleans recording whether truncation or redaction occurred.
close_reason: Implemented runner argv/shell validation, env injection, timeout/capture/redaction handling, and unsandboxed-runner warning support — commit 449ded0

title: Capture workspace manifests
description: The core differentiator is scoring the resulting workspace, so evalctl must capture structured before/after filesystem evidence rather than relying on textual diffs.
design: Walk the per-case workspace before and after runner execution to produce `workspace-before.json` and `workspace-after.json`. Derive `workspace-diff.json` from those manifests. Include untracked and ignored files. Represent files, directories, symlinks, and other special file types. Use POSIX-style relative UTF-8 paths with no `.` or `..` segments and no absolute paths.
acceptance_criteria:
- Full manifests contain entries with `path`, `kind`, and file hashes where applicable.
- Directories are represented by presence; binary files are represented by sha256; symlinks are not followed and store target information.
- Unreadable or unsupported non-UTF-8 paths emit `W_PATH_UNREADABLE` and do not silently corrupt the manifest.
- `workspace-diff.json` identifies added, modified, and deleted paths from the two structured manifests.
- Textual `workspace.diff` is best-effort and never parsed by scorers.
close_reason: Implemented before/after workspace manifests, structured diff manifests, path normalization, symlink/special-file handling, and text diff projection — commit 449ded0

title: Implement deterministic built-in scorers
description: v0.1 must grade runs with deterministic local scorers that are credible without an LLM judge and can be recomputed from persisted artifacts.
design: Implement built-in scorers for `exact`, `contains`, `regex`, `json-schema`, `numeric-threshold`, `file-exists`, `exit-code`, and `workspace-diff`. Each scorer emits `{ok, score, label, findings}` and respects whether it is required or advisory. Built-in scorers consume persisted, redacted outputs and structured workspace manifests.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each scorer has unit tests for pass, fail, and malformed-input behavior.
- `workspace-diff` matches `expect.files_changed` and `expect.files_forbidden` using glob semantics against `changed_paths[].path`.
- `exit-code` compares expected exit code against `runner.json` and does not conflate failed expectations with tool errors.
- Required scorer failures produce case status `fail`; scorer crashes or invalid scorer inputs produce case status `error`.
- Score output is stable and can be serialized into each case `score.json`.
close_reason: Implemented deterministic built-in scorers for text, regex, exact, JSON parse, numeric threshold, file existence, exit code, and workspace diff — commit 449ded0

title: Implement synchronous run orchestration
description: v0.1 needs one complete synchronous execution path that can run a suite, invoke runners, score cases, and continue through partial failures without depending on async infrastructure.
design:
Implement `evalctl run <suite> [--jobs N] [--timeout S] [--run-id <id>] [--fail-on-fail] [--json]`. Create a reservation for the run id, materialize a fresh workspace per case, execute cases with bounded concurrency, write artifacts, derive scores, update `manifest.json` atomically, and continue after case-level errors with `W_PARTIAL_RUN`.

Default `--jobs` to `min(CPU_count, 4)`. Sort iteration before serialization so JSON is deterministic regardless of completion order. Use `<UTC-timestamp>-<suite-name>` for default run ids. Reusing a completed matching run id returns the existing run; live reservations return `E_RUN_BUSY`; semantic clashes return `E_RUN_CONFLICT`.
acceptance_criteria:
- `run` produces a complete run directory under `evals/runs/` with a suite snapshot and per-case artifacts.
- Case errors do not abort the whole run; the run remains reportable and emits `W_PARTIAL_RUN`.
- Eval failures exit 0 by default and set `data.run.ok:false`; `--fail-on-fail` exits 6 when any case is not `pass`.
- A live reservation returns exit 4 with `E_RUN_BUSY` and a retry recommendation; a completed mismatched run id returns exit 5 with `E_RUN_CONFLICT`.
- JSON output includes paste-ready follow-up commands only for implemented verbs.
close_reason: Implemented synchronous run orchestration with per-case workspaces, run directories, scoring, partial-run warnings, run-id reuse, and fail-on-fail exit behavior — commit 449ded0

title: Build portable run directory model
description: The run directory is the v0.1 source of truth, so it must carry everything needed to inspect, report, and re-score a completed run without relying on shell history or the original suite location.
design: Write `manifest.json`, `suite-snapshot/`, and per-case `input.json`, `task.txt`, `runner.json`, stdout/stderr captures, `output.*`, before/after workspace manifests, derived `workspace-diff.json`, best-effort `workspace.diff`, and `score.json`. Keep every path recorded inside the run directory relative to the run-directory root. Treat `report.md` as a convenience copy; regenerate authoritative reports from manifest and artifacts.
acceptance_criteria:
- No artifact path inside `manifest.json`, score files, or report payloads is absolute.
- `suite-snapshot/` is sufficient for `status` and `report` to interpret scorer configuration from a copied run directory.
- `created_ts` and run ids are treated as volatile metadata and excluded from canonical report hashes.
- `score.json` is persisted for inspection but is not trusted as input during artifact replay.
- The run directory layout is documented by `robot-docs guide`.
close_reason: Implemented portable run directory layout with manifest, suite snapshot, per-case artifacts, relative manifest paths, and replay-safe score recomputation — commit 449ded0

title: Implement status and report commands
description: Agents need diagnose and triage commands that summarize run state, rank failures deterministically, and point to the exact artifacts needed for inspection.
design:
Implement `status <run-id|--run-dir <path>> [--json]` and `report <run-id|--run-dir <path>> [--format markdown|json] [--json]`. Resolve run ids under `evals/runs/`; accept copied standalone run directories through `--run-dir`. Rank report failures as `error` before `fail`, then by ascending aggregate numeric score, then case id.

`status` should include per-case state and a `recommended_action`. `report` should include aggregate scores, ranked failures, relative artifact links, and `data.report_hash` over the normalized report projection.
acceptance_criteria:
- `status` works for both local run ids and copied run directories.
- `report --format json` and `report --json` both return the universal envelope.
- Markdown reports are deterministic apart from explicitly volatile metadata.
- Ranked failures are ordered by error/fail class, aggregate score, and case id.
- `commands[]` contains only implemented follow-up commands such as regenerating a JSON report.
close_reason: Implemented status and report commands for run ids and copied run directories with ranked failures, report_hash, markdown, and JSON envelopes — commit 449ded0

title: Add real-spoolctl CI coverage
description:
Queued-run semantics are verified in CI only against a fake spoolctl fixture.
That fixture is built from evalctl's own expectations, so by construction it
cannot notice when the real tool's contract moves — which is how a contract bump
broke every queued run and stayed undetected across nine spoolctl releases.

A compatibility fix whose only evidence is the fixture that missed the
incompatibility is not proven. Real-binary coverage closes the blind spot that
produced the outage.

Do not release v0.4.2 until this epic is merged and passing in CI. This is a
release blocker, not merely a dependent task: dependency order makes it next,
but only an explicit stop makes it required.
acceptance_criteria:
- Queued-run semantics are exercised against a real pinned spoolctl in CI.
- The job cannot pass by skipping its tests.
- Local test discovery is unaffected when spoolctl is not installed.
- v0.4.2 is not released until this epic is merged and passing.

title: Add real-spoolctl integration test module
description:
No test drives evalctl's queued path against a real spoolctl binary. Every
queued behavior evalctl depends on — outcome mapping, artifact reconstruction,
report determinism — is currently verified only against a fixture that agrees
with evalctl by construction.
design:
Add a test module driving the installed spoolctl binary. Coverage:

    queued vs in-process report-hash parity
    queue provenance in the run manifest
    nonzero runner exit scored, not reported as an infrastructure error
    runner timeout mapped to E_RUNNER_TIMEOUT
    spawn failure mapped to E_RUNNER_FAILED
    the stdin:"task" runner wrapper
    resume after an interrupted queued run

Nonzero-exit scoring earns its place: conflating a failing task with broken
infrastructure would silently corrupt eval results rather than error loudly.

The module skips when spoolctl is absent so local discovery is unaffected. An
environment variable, set only in CI, converts a missing or below-floor binary
into a hard failure at import.

Keep any test-helper sharing to the minimum this module needs. A general
refactor of the existing CLI test helpers is separate work and must not ride
along here.
acceptance_criteria:
- All listed behaviors are exercised against the real binary and pass.
- The module skips cleanly when spoolctl is absent.
- With the CI environment variable set and spoolctl missing or below the floor,
  the module fails with a message naming the required version.
- No unrelated refactor of existing test modules is included.
close_reason: Added tests/test_real_spoolctl.py (commit 5e62569), 10 tests driving the installed spoolctl binary rather than the fake fixture. Covers all seven behaviors from the design plus three that fell out of it: the advertised floor is satisfiable by a published release, and capabilities and doctor both report the observed version and contract. Skip/hard-fail contract works in all four combinations, each verified by hand: spoolctl absent and EVALCTL_REQUIRE_REAL_SPOOLCTL unset skips 10; absent with the variable set raises at import naming the cause and the fix; a below-floor 0.4.4 binary with the variable set raises naming the observed version and the floor; below-floor without the variable skips. The version and contract under test are printed to stderr at import so a CI log records what it proved. Full discovery: 96 tests OK with real spoolctl 0.4.11 on PATH and the variable set (2 skips, both pre-existing and unrelated), 96 OK with spoolctl absent (12 skips). Ran the new module three times for flakiness; stable. No shared test-helper refactor: the CLI helpers are a small local harness, and the reason is recorded in a comment at the class so a later reader does not read the duplication as an oversight. One design correction found while writing: the resume test's reference run must be taken after the slow runner fixtures are installed, or the hash comparison fails on a fixture difference rather than on the interruption. The test also asserts a case was genuinely left unfinished, so it cannot pass on a run that had already completed.

title: Add queue-integration CI job with hard guard
description:
Real-binary tests that no CI job runs provide no protection. The job must also
be unable to report success while silently skipping the tests it exists to run —
a self-skipping job would reproduce the original blind spot in a form that looks
green.
design:
Add a `queue-integration` job to the CI workflow: checkout, set up Python,
install pinned `spoolctl==0.4.11`, print the spoolctl version and contract under
test for the log record, then run the real-spoolctl test module with the
require-real-spoolctl environment variable set.

The pin uses `spoolctl==0.4.11` as the reproducible input and deliberately adds
no separate hash pin in this release; PyPI publishes only that release and one
alpha, so the version pin is unambiguous. Recording the decision here prevents a
future reviewer treating the absent checksum as an oversight.

Failure rule:

    Local: spoolctl absent            -> skip
    CI:    spoolctl absent or too old -> hard failure
acceptance_criteria:
- A `queue-integration` job exists and runs the real-spoolctl tests.
- The job installs `spoolctl==0.4.11` and logs the version and contract tested.
- The require-real-spoolctl variable is set in the job environment.
- Removing spoolctl from the job makes it fail rather than skip.
- The workflow file parses and the existing test job is unchanged.
close_reason: Added the queue-integration job to .github/workflows/ci.yml (commit 121dac1). Steps: checkout, setup-python 3.11, pip install 'spoolctl==0.4.11', 'spoolctl capabilities --json' as the log record of the version and contract under test, then 'python -m unittest tests.test_real_spoolctl -v' with EVALCTL_REQUIRE_REAL_SPOOLCTL=1. The variable is what makes the job unfalsifiable: a missing or below-floor binary fails at import instead of skipping to a green result. Chose Python 3.11, the oldest supported runtime, and confirmed spoolctl 0.4.11 declares Requires-Python >=3.10 so the pin installs there. Dropped a 'spoolctl --version || true' logging line in favour of the capabilities envelope alone - it carries both tool_version and contract_version, so no step needs a failure-swallowing fudge. The absent hash pin is documented inline as a decision. The existing test job is unchanged; git diff shows the workflow change is purely additive. Verified locally by running the job's exact test command with the variable set and spoolctl on PATH (10 tests OK) and by parsing the workflow as YAML to confirm both jobs and all step names resolve.

title: Bound the per-case collections in plan, status and report; reject bad cursors
description:
Closes findings F5 and F4 of the v0.4.3 make-cli conformance sweep.

Exactly one verb carries bounding flags:

    $ evalctl capabilities --json | jq '[.data.verbs | to_entries[]
        | select((.value.flags // []) | index("--limit") or index("--cursor")) | .key]'
    ["jobs"]

Exactly three verbs return an unbounded per-case collection: `plan`, `status`
and `report`. That is the complete list -- `validate` and `run` return
summaries, and `doctor`'s seven components are a fixed vocabulary rather than
an input-scaled collection.

`plan` is the one that hurts, at roughly 660 bytes per case against `status`'s
58. On a 402-case suite:

    $ evalctl plan <suite> --json | wc -c
      257612
    $ evalctl plan <suite> --json | jq '.meta.pagination, .meta.truncated'
    null
    null
    $ evalctl plan <suite> --limit 10 --json
    unknown flag '--limit'

A quarter of a megabyte in one envelope, no truncation notice, and the bounding
flag rejected. `determinism.md` calls unbounded list output a denial of service
against agent context windows.

F4 is the same surface from the other side: `jobs list --cursor garbage`
returns exit 0 with `ok: true` and zero rows, which is indistinguishable from
an empty page. A cursor the tool did not issue is a user-input error.
design:
The `jobs list` implementation is already the right shape -- bounded default,
`--limit`, `--cursor`, `meta.pagination` and `meta.truncated`. This is
extending a working in-house pattern to three more verbs, not designing one.

Default bound, explicit `--limit` override, and a cursor for the next page.
When the bound clips, say so in `meta.truncated` with the omitted count, and
put the paste-ready next-page command in `commands`.

For F4, an unparseable or unissued cursor should be `E_CASE_INVALID` at exit 1
with the offending value named, matching how the tool already treats other
malformed documented inputs since v0.4.1.
acceptance_criteria:
- `plan`, `status` and `report` each accept `--limit` and a cursor, and apply a documented default bound.
- When the bound clips, `meta.truncated` reports the omitted count and `commands` carries the next-page invocation.
- The default and maximum for each verb are documented in `capabilities`, as they already are for `jobs`.
- On a suite large enough to clip, paging through with the cursor yields every case exactly once. Asserted by a test, not by inspection.
- `jobs list --cursor <unissued>` returns `E_CASE_INVALID` at exit 1 naming the value, and no longer returns zero rows as success.
- An unbounded call on a small suite returns the same bytes as today, so existing goldens do not churn.
close_reason: Bounded plan/status/report per-case collections with --limit/--cursor + meta.pagination/truncated via shared paginate_cases; unissued cursor now E_CASE_INVALID on all four paginated verbs (F4/F5). Commit 3a42974.

title: Add a bulk or stdin path for case add
description:
Closes finding F19 of the v0.4.3 make-cli conformance sweep.

There is no bulk or stdin path for `case add`. Authoring a forty-case suite is
forty invocations, each paying full process startup and each a separate
opportunity to fail halfway. During the sweep a forty-case suite was built
exactly this way, which is what surfaced the gap.

Low weight for this archetype and a real gap. `composability.md` asks for a
stdin path wherever pipelining makes sense, and generating cases from a data
file is the obvious case for it.
design:
Accept case records on stdin, one JSON object per line, matching the shape
`cases.jsonl` already uses on disk -- so a suite's own case file round-trips
through the verb without transformation.

Bulk creation is not transactional by nature, so the envelope needs to report
per-record outcomes rather than a single boolean: which ids were created, which
were skipped as duplicates, and which were rejected and why. An agent piping
300 records needs to know which ones landed.
acceptance_criteria:
- `case add` accepts records on stdin, one JSON object per line, in the same shape as `cases.jsonl`.
- A suite's existing `cases.jsonl` can be piped into a fresh suite and produces an equivalent suite.
- The envelope reports created, skipped and rejected counts, and names each rejected record with its reason.
- A partial failure is reported as a partial failure, not as a single pass or fail.
- The exit code for a partial failure follows whatever the exit-code contract bead decides.
- Grammar tests cover empty stdin, a malformed line among good lines, a duplicate id, and a trailing newline.
close_reason: Added case add --stdin bulk path (commit 296a88a): whole-record stdin, per-record added/skipped/rejected report, W_CASE_ADD_REJECTED, atomic append, grammar + round-trip tests. Closes F19.

title: Decide the contract_version type before a 1.0
description:
Closes finding F21 of the v0.4.3 make-cli conformance sweep.

`contract_version` is the integer `1` where the contract assumes a dotted
string. The compatibility check in the reference material splits the field on
`.` and would raise against evalctl's value.

The concrete cost is that there is no minor channel. v0.2, v0.3 and v0.4 were
all additive and all had to stay at `1`, so an agent cannot tell those three
contracts apart through the field that exists for exactly that purpose. It has
to infer capability from `tool_version` or by probing for verbs.

Changing the type is itself a breaking change for anything that reads the
field, which is why this wants deciding before a 1.0 rather than after.
design:
Three options, in rough order of preference.

Move to a dotted string, `"1.0"`, and bump the minor on every additive change.
This matches the reference's compatibility idiom directly and gives agents the
channel they need. It breaks any consumer doing an integer comparison, which is
the cost, and it is cheapest to pay now.

Or keep the integer as a major and add a separate additive counter alongside
it, which avoids breaking existing readers at the cost of a second field to
explain.

Or keep the integer and document plainly that additive change is not signalled
in the contract, so agents must probe. Honest, and the weakest of the three.

Whichever is chosen, the reasoning belongs in the CHANGELOG, since this is the
field that tells consumers what the CHANGELOG means.
acceptance_criteria:
- A decision is recorded in the CHANGELOG with its reasoning.
- If the type changes, `capabilities`, every schema, all goldens and the docs move together, and the change is called out as breaking.
- If the type does not change, the documented compatibility guidance says what an agent should do to detect an additive change.
- The rule for when the field moves is stated somewhere an agent can read, not only in a commit message.
- A test asserts the field's type matches what `capabilities` documents.
close_reason: Adopted dotted MAJOR.MINOR string contract_version ("1.0"): capabilities schema typed string with pattern, data+meta+all schemas+goldens+docs/agent-guide.md moved together, test asserts value type matches capabilities. Breaking, decided pre-1.0. Commit 047ae5b.

title: Align the DIAGNOSE payload and the feedback fields with the reference shapes
description:
Closes findings F10, F11 and F9 of the v0.4.3 make-cli conformance sweep.

Three cosmetic divergences, each cheap alone and worth one pass together. All
sit on axes the archetype weights -- DIAGNOSE high, feedback low -- but none
causes a wrong answer, which is why they rank low despite the axis.

F10. `doctor.operation_outcome` diverges from the DIAGNOSE reference shape.

F11. `status` carries a `recommended_action` inside `data` while leaving the
envelope's `commands` array empty. The reference puts paste-ready commands in
`commands` precisely so an agent does not have to know which verb hides them
where. `doctor` already does this correctly, so the two verbs disagree with
each other.

F9. inferctl degradation is reported as a warning only, and `meta` carries no
requested-versus-actual mode. An agent that asked for inferctl provenance and
silently got none cannot tell from `meta` that it was downgraded.

Worth recording alongside these: the inferctl doctor probe itself is sound. It
was exercised through all four of its states during the sweep -- route present,
preflight without route, no preflight, and binary absent -- and each is
distinguishable, with `route_available` flipping to false rather than
disappearing.
design:
Bring `doctor.operation_outcome` to the reference field names.

Populate `commands` on `status` with the same paste-ready strings
`recommended_action` already implies, matching what `doctor` does. Keep
`recommended_action` in `data`; this is an addition, not a move.

Add requested-versus-actual mode provenance to `meta` when inferctl capture is
requested and not delivered, so a degraded run is detectable without parsing
warning text.
acceptance_criteria:
- `doctor.operation_outcome` matches the DIAGNOSE reference field names, and the golden is re-pinned.
- `status` populates `commands` with paste-ready invocations consistent with its `recommended_action`.
- `doctor` and `status` use the same convention for where follow-up commands live.
- When inferctl provenance is requested and not captured, `meta` carries the requested mode and the actual mode.
- A test asserts the degraded path sets both, rather than relying on the warning being present.
- Changes to `doctor` output are reflected in its schema and golden.
close_reason: Aligned doctor.operation_outcome to DIAGNOSE reference (exit_code_kind + next_check_after_seconds), surfaced status recommended_action in commands[], added run/replay meta.inferctl requested-vs-actual pair. Commit 792bf8a.

title: Adopt spoolctl failure_reason in queued runs
description:
Queued-run classification in `runner_result_from_spoolctl_attempt`
(`evalctl/runner.py:264`) infers *why* an attempt ended from two proxies that
evalctl does not own:

    timed_out = state == "timed_out" and exit_code is None
    spawn_failed = exit_code is None and (state in {"failed", "abandoned", "canceled"}
                                          or str(attempt.get("error") or "").startswith("spawn failed:"))

Both exist because spoolctl 0.4.1 had no machine-readable failure enum. It has
had one since 0.4.2, and since evalctl v0.4.2 the floor guarantees it: contract
>= 2 is required, every spoolctl at that contract advertises `failure_reasons`
in `capabilities` and emits `attempts[].failure_reason`, and the probe enforces
this on every queued run.

Two defects:

- Fragility. A prefix match on a human error string is a contract spoolctl can
  reword in any release. Nothing would fail loudly; evalctl would silently
  reclassify a spawn failure as a clean exit. The state-set proxy has the same
  shape.
- A live bug. `runner.py:280` reads `attempt.get("duration_ms")`, a field real
  spoolctl never emits, so **every queued case records `duration_ms: 0`**.
  Observed on the scaffolded suite: queued `cr-fail`/`cr-pass` both `0`;
  the same suite in-process, `14` and `15`.

Why the tests did not catch the duration bug, which is the part worth
remembering: the fake fixture emits `duration_ms` (`tests/fakes.py:125`)
because it was written against evalctl's expectations rather than spoolctl's
output. The real-spoolctl job would only catch it if something asserted on
duration, and nothing does. Report-hash parity did not catch it and
structurally cannot -- `duration_ms` lives only in `cases/<id>/runner.json`,
appearing in neither `case_manifest_entry` (`evalctl/scoring.py`) nor the
report projection (`evalctl/reports.py`). The queued run reproduced the exact
v0.4.2 report hash while carrying wrong durations in every case. Hash parity
proves the scored projection agrees; it says nothing about artifact fidelity
outside it.

Scoped honestly: this is mostly a robustness deletion. For every outcome
evalctl can reach today, old and new classification agree -- `spawn_failed`
and `worker_crash` land where the old state-set landed, `timeout` matches,
`process_exit` with a concrete exit code matches. The value is one owned
contract instead of two borrowed proxies, less code, and the `duration_ms`
fix, which is the only real behavior change. Do not write a changelog entry
implying queued runs were misclassifying outcomes; nothing observed shows that.

This epic is the whole of release v0.4.3.
design:
Evidence gathered against real spoolctl 0.4.11 (`.venv/bin/spoolctl` inside
the project checkout; it is not on PATH), by driving four jobs to terminal
states:

| job | attempt `state` | `exit_code` | `failure_reason` | job `state` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `echo hi` | succeeded | 0 | null | done |
| `exit 7` | failed | 7 | process_exit | dead |
| `sleep 5`, timeout 1 | timed_out | null | timeout | dead |
| `/nonexistent/binary` | failed | null | spawn_failed | dead |

A *successful* attempt carries `failure_reason: null`, not `process_exit`.
`process_exit` means the process ran and its exit code is the fact, pass or
fail. Job state for failures is `dead`, never `failed`.

`capabilities --json` advertises `failure_reasons: [process_exit, timeout,
spawn_failed, worker_crash, canceled, unknown]`.

Full real attempt key set: `attempt_no, error, exit_code, failure_reason,
finished_at, started_at, state, stderr_path, stdout_path, worker_id,
worker_pid`. `started_at`/`finished_at` are epoch-second floats.

Base for implementation: current `main` head (`e91d73b`, `v0.4.2-3`), which
carries the trusted-publishing workflow, the `.DS_Store` ignore and the PyPI

title: Correct the fake spoolctl attempt payload to the real field set
description:
The fake spoolctl in `tests/fakes.py` synthesizes an attempt record written
from evalctl's expectations rather than from spoolctl's real output. It emits
`duration_ms` (`tests/fakes.py:125`), a field real spoolctl 0.4.11 never
emits, and omits `failure_reason`, which real spoolctl always emits. That
divergence is what hid the live `duration_ms: 0` bug from the entire suite --
the same blind-spot class as the earlier contract-version outage.

Separately, four `failure_reason` values -- `worker_crash`, `canceled`,
`unknown`, and any future member -- cannot be produced by the real binary in
CI. The fake must be able to synthesize them, which is precisely the
synthetic-failure role the fake was narrowed to.
design:
Real attempt key set to match: `attempt_no, error, exit_code, failure_reason,
finished_at, started_at, state, stderr_path, stdout_path, worker_id,
worker_pid`. `started_at`/`finished_at` are epoch-second floats.

Reason values follow the real binary: `None` on success, `process_exit` on
nonzero exit, `timeout`, `spawn_failed`.

Control surface, named now so it cannot grow ad hoc. Two environment variables
read by the fake's `work` path, following the existing `FAKE_SPOOLCTL_TRANSIENT`
precedent (`tests/fakes.py:80`):

    FAKE_SPOOLCTL_FAILURE_REASON=<string>   override the synthesized failure_reason
    FAKE_SPOOLCTL_EXIT_CODE=<int|empty>     override the synthesized exit_code
                                            (empty string means null)

Environment variables rather than `install_fake_spoolctl` kwargs, because one
installed fake must vary per invocation within a single test, and because
`work` is spawned by evalctl and inherits the test process environment.

Binding constraint: these override **only the synthesized attempt record**.
They must not change whether or how the real subprocess runs. If they do, the
fake stops being a fake of spoolctl and becomes a fake of the test's
expectations -- the exact failure this work exists to undo.

Sequencing note: dropping `duration_ms` from the fake breaks the current
`runner.py:280` read until the duration task lands. Commit the two together if
the tree must stay green at every commit.
acceptance_criteria:
- The fake's attempt record carries `failure_reason`, `started_at` and
  `finished_at`, and no longer carries `duration_ms`.
- The payload matches real spoolctl 0.4.11 field-for-field for every field
  evalctl reads.
- Synthesized reasons match the real binary: `None` on success, `process_exit`
  on nonzero exit, `timeout` on timeout, `spawn_failed` on spawn failure.
- `FAKE_SPOOLCTL_FAILURE_REASON` overrides the synthesized reason, including
  with a value that is not a known enum member.
- `FAKE_SPOOLCTL_EXIT_CODE` overrides the synthesized exit code; an empty
  string yields a null `exit_code`.
- Neither variable changes whether or how the subprocess runs -- demonstrated
  by a test that sets a knob and still observes the real command's stdout.
close_reason: Fake spoolctl now synthesizes the real 0.4.11 attempt key set (attempt_no, error, exit_code, failure_reason, finished_at, started_at, state, stderr_path, stdout_path, worker_id, worker_pid); duration_ms is gone. Reasons match the real binary: null on success, process_exit, timeout, spawn_failed. FAKE_SPOOLCTL_FAILURE_REASON and FAKE_SPOOLCTL_EXIT_CODE override only the synthesized record, applied after the subprocess runs; a test sets each knob and still reads the real command's stdout. Fake and real binary are both asserted against the shared REAL_SPOOLCTL_ATTEMPT_KEYS constant, so drift on either side fails. Also made the fake's stream paths absolute, matching real spoolctl. Commit 139c4e9.

title: Key queued classification on failure_reason and exit_code
description:
`runner_result_from_spoolctl_attempt` (`evalctl/runner.py:264`) decides
`timed_out` and `spawn_failed` from the attempt's `state` field and from a
prefix match on `attempt["error"]` against the literal `spawn failed:`. Both
are contracts evalctl does not own: spoolctl can reword the error string or
change its state vocabulary in any release, and evalctl would not fail loudly
-- it would silently reclassify a spawn failure as a clean exit.

spoolctl has emitted a machine-readable `attempts[].failure_reason` since
0.4.2, and evalctl's v0.4.2 floor (contract >= 2) guarantees it is present on
every queued run. The proxies have no remaining justification.
design:
Replace the two proxies with a lookup keyed on the pair
`(failure_reason, exit_code)`. No row consults attempt `state`.

| `failure_reason` | `exit_code` | `timed_out` | `spawn_failed` | resulting `error_code` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| null / absent | 0 | False | False | none -- score normally |
| null / absent | nonzero or absent | False | True | E_RUNNER_FAILED |
| process_exit | concrete | False | False | none -- score normally |
| process_exit | absent (malformed) | False | True | E_RUNNER_FAILED |
| timeout | any | True | False | E_RUNNER_TIMEOUT |
| spawn_failed | any | False | True | E_RUNNER_FAILED |
| worker_crash | any | False | True | E_RUNNER_FAILED |
| canceled | any | False | True | E_RUNNER_FAILED |
| unknown | any | False | True | E_RUNNER_FAILED |
| anything else | any | False | True | E_RUNNER_FAILED |

Rows 2 and 4 are the defensive pair. Neither is reachable from any observed
spoolctl behavior; both exist so a payload that contradicts its own contract
cannot produce a pass. Row 2 is the one worth arguing about, since it sends a
*nonzero exit* to the infrastructure-error class rather than scoring it, the
opposite of what evalctl does everywhere else. It is correct here: real
spoolctl always sets `process_exit` alongside a nonzero exit code, so a null
reason with a nonzero exit is malformed data, not a failing case. Conservative
in the direction that cannot manufacture a false pass.

The last row is the forward-compatibility rule: an unrecognized reason is
treated as `unknown`, not as an error. A sibling tool adding an enum member
must not take evalctl down.

Delete, do not demote to a fallback:
- the `state == "timed_out"` test,
- the `state in {"failed", "abandoned", "canceled"}` set,
- the `str(attempt.get("error") or "").startswith("spawn failed:")` prefix match.

`attempt.get("error")` stays as the `stderr` fallback when no `stderr_path`
exists (`runner.py:268`) -- that is display text, not classification.

`error_code` is still derived downstream in `normalize_runner_artifacts`
(`runner.py:180`) from `timed_out`/`spawn_failed`; that line does not change.
`exit_code` is carried through to `runner.json` unchanged in every row.

Add a comment at the mapping stating *why* classification keys on the enum, so
a future reader does not "restore" the state check as a safety net.

Known constraint, recorded here deliberately and **not** work for this task:
`latest_terminal_attempt` (`runner.py:257`) takes `attempts[-1]` rather than
the attempt with the highest `attempt_no`. Equivalent while evalctl passes
`--max-retries 0`. If retries are ever enabled, this becomes a bug.
acceptance_criteria:
- Classification reads only `failure_reason` and `exit_code` from the attempt;
  the attempt's `state` is not consulted anywhere in the function.
- All three deleted proxies are gone from `evalctl/runner.py`, not kept as
  fallbacks.
- `grep -r "spawn failed:" evalctl/` finds nothing outside `scoring.py`'s own
  command-scorer message.
- An unrecognized `failure_reason` yields `E_RUNNER_FAILED`, never
  `E_SPOOLCTL_INCOMPATIBLE`.
- A comment at the mapping explains why the enum is the key and warns against
  restoring the state check.
- No new error code, exit code, case status, or envelope field.
close_reason: classify_spoolctl_attempt(failure_reason, exit_code) in evalctl/runner.py implements all ten rows; attempt state is not consulted in runner_result_from_spoolctl_attempt. All three proxies deleted, not demoted: the state == timed_out test, the state in {failed, abandoned, canceled} set, and the 'spawn failed:' prefix match. grep -r 'spawn failed:' evalctl/ now finds only scoring.py:189, the command-scorer message. Unrecognized reasons fall through to E_RUNNER_FAILED, never E_SPOOLCTL_INCOMPATIBLE. Docstring at the mapping states why the enum is the key, warns against restoring the state check, and names the two counter-intuitive rows. No new error code, exit code, case status, or envelope field. Full suite green (99 tests, 2 skipped) with real spoolctl 0.4.11 on PATH. Commit 7127cd8. Bool-typed exit codes are excluded from the concrete-exit test so a JSON false cannot take the pass row. Row-by-row test coverage is evalctl-ede.4.

title: Compute queued duration_ms from attempt timestamps
description:
`runner.py:280` computes `int(attempt.get("duration_ms") or 0)`. Real spoolctl
0.4.11 attempts have no `duration_ms` field, so the expression is always `0`
and **every queued case records `duration_ms: 0`**.

Confirmed end to end on the scaffolded suite:

    queued  (--queue spoolctl):  cr-fail duration_ms=0    cr-pass duration_ms=0
    in-process (same suite):     cr-fail duration_ms=14   cr-pass duration_ms=15

Real timings are recoverable: `started_at` and `finished_at` are epoch-second
floats present on every attempt.
design:
duration_ms = max(0, round((finished_at - started_at) * 1000))
                  when both are numeric; else 0

No fallback to reading `duration_ms` from the attempt. Keeping the read, and
having the fake keep emitting the field, preserves exactly the divergence that
hid this bug for two releases.
acceptance_criteria:
- `duration_ms` on a queued case is derived from `finished_at - started_at`.
- The `attempt.get("duration_ms")` read is gone from `evalctl/runner.py`.
- Reversed timestamps clamp to `0`; a missing timestamp on either side gives
  `0`.
- Report hashes are unchanged by this fix (`duration_ms` is not in the report
  projection), verified against a pre-change run.

title: Unit coverage for every classification row
description:
The new `(failure_reason, exit_code)` classification has ten rows, four of
which cannot be produced by the real spoolctl binary in CI (`worker_crash`,
`canceled`, `unknown`, and any unrecognized future value) and two more of
which are defensive rows that no observed spoolctl behavior reaches. Without
fake-driven coverage, most of the mapping ships unexercised -- which is how
the previous classification path went two releases with a silent bug.
design:
Drive every row through the fake, using the `FAKE_SPOOLCTL_FAILURE_REASON` and
`FAKE_SPOOLCTL_EXIT_CODE` knobs. Assert on `runner.json`'s `error_code`,
`timed_out` and `spawn_failed`, and on the case status in the envelope.

Rows to cover: null reason with exit 0; null reason with nonzero exit; null
reason with absent exit; `process_exit` with a concrete exit code;
`process_exit` with no exit code; `timeout`; `spawn_failed`; `worker_crash`;
`canceled`; `unknown`; plus a made-up value that is not a known enum member.

Also cover duration through the fake: known `started_at`/`finished_at` yields
the expected `duration_ms`; reversed timestamps clamp to `0`; missing
timestamps give `0`.

Name the two counter-intuitive rows explicitly in the test names, because they
are the ones a future reader will assume are wrong:
- null reason with a nonzero exit is `E_RUNNER_FAILED`, not a scored failure;
- `process_exit` with no exit code is `E_RUNNER_FAILED`, not a pass.
acceptance_criteria:
- All ten mapping rows have a fake-driven test, including the unrecognized
  future value.
- The unrecognized value asserts `E_RUNNER_FAILED` and specifically asserts
  that `E_SPOOLCTL_INCOMPATIBLE` is not raised.
- The two counter-intuitive rows are covered by tests whose names say what
  they pin.
- Duration cases covered: expected value, reversed clamp to `0`, missing
  timestamps to `0`.
- The existing real-spoolctl timeout and spawn-failure tests pass unedited.

Driving them through the fake would need a timestamp knob, growing a control surface evalctl-ede.1 fixed on purpose, to synthesize records no spoolctl emits. title: Assert real queued duration against the real spoolctl binary
description:
Nothing in the suite asserts on a queued case's duration against the real
binary, which is the single missing assertion that would have caught every
queued case recording `duration_ms: 0`. Fake coverage alone cannot catch it,
because the fake is what diverged in the first place. Report-hash parity
cannot catch it either -- `duration_ms` is absent from the report projection,
and the buggy queued run reproduced the correct v0.4.2 hash.
design:
In the real-spoolctl job, queue a case that sleeps `0.5s`, then assert
`400 <= duration_ms < 10000`.

Fixed bounds, deliberately. The lower bound proves real elapsed time is
recorded; the ceiling stops a hung environment from passing. A relative
comparison against the in-process duration was considered and rejected: it
drifts with timer noise, and it is too loose to fail if a hard-coded zero were
ever replaced by a hard-coded small constant. Keep the in-process value in the
failure message as a diagnostic, never as a pass condition.
acceptance_criteria:
- A real-spoolctl test queues a `0.5s` sleep and asserts
  `400 <= duration_ms < 10000`.
- The assertion fails if `duration_ms` is `0`, verified by running it against
  the pre-fix code once.
- No in-process duration comparison appears in the pass condition.

The in-process duration is captured only for the failure message; it is not in any pass condition. Verified the assertion bites: reverting evalctl/runner.py to the pre-fix attempt.get('duration_ms') read makes it fail with 'queued duration 0ms; in-process was 526ms'; restored and re-verified green. title: Complete the valid sets and exit codes on three error paths
description:
Closes findings F7, F17 and F20 of the v0.4.3 make-cli conformance sweep.

Three sites, one omission. `errors.md` requires an error to name the failure,
the valid set, the corrected command, and a safe alternative.

F7. `E_RUN_NOT_FOUND` and `E_SUITE_NOT_FOUND` omit the valid set and hint at
the wrong command. Both valid sets are small and already on disk -- the run
directories and the suite directories -- so the tool can list them.

F17. `init` on an unwritable directory returns a wrong, undeclared error rather
than a permission failure at the declared exit code.

F20. `schema <unknown-verb>` returns `E_CASE_INVALID` with no `valid_values`
and no `did_you_mean`, from the verb whose entire job is exporting the
contract and whose valid set is the fifteen verb names it already holds.
`E_UNKNOWN_COMMAND` is the right code there.

The tool already implements the correct pattern twice, in `doctor --component`
and in the unknown-flag errors. This is copying an in-house pattern to three
more sites, not inventing one.
design:
For each of the three sites, populate `valid_values` from the set the tool
already has, add `did_you_mean` where an edit-distance match exists, and make
the `hint` name a command that would actually help.

For `init` on an unwritable path, return the declared tool-environment error at
its declared exit code.

For `schema`, change the code to `E_UNKNOWN_COMMAND` and carry the fifteen verb
names.

One caution observed during the sweep and worth honoring here: a suggestion
that crosses between unrelated flags is worse than no suggestion. `--limit` on
`plan` is corrected to `--timeout`, which is a valid command with unrelated
semantics; an agent that pastes it gets a working invocation that does not do
what it asked. Where the suggestion machinery reaches across unrelated
semantics, prefer no suggestion.
acceptance_criteria:
- `E_RUN_NOT_FOUND` carries the known run ids, or a bounded sample plus a count, and hints at a command that lists them.
- `E_SUITE_NOT_FOUND` carries the known suite names and a `did_you_mean` when one is close.
- `init` on an unwritable directory returns the declared tool-environment error at its declared exit code, with a message naming the path problem.
- `schema <unknown-verb>` returns `E_UNKNOWN_COMMAND` carrying all fifteen verb names.

title: Decide and implement the exit-code contract for exits 2 and 6
description:
Closes findings F2 and F22 of the v0.4.3 make-cli conformance sweep, and
answers the question already tracked separately as the doctor exit-code
contract.

Two halves of one question: what the published exit dictionary promises versus
what the tool actually emits.

Half one, F2. `run --fail-on-fail` exits 6 and writes nothing anywhere:

    run <suite> --fail-on-fail   exit=6  ok=true  errors=[]  stderr=0 bytes

A non-zero exit with `ok: true`, an empty `errors` list, and an empty stderr.
The before-ship rule is that every failure produces a diagnostic on stderr and
a non-zero exit; this produces the exit and no diagnostic. `envelope.md` is
explicit that `ok` is false on any failure and `errors` is non-empty on
failure. An agent that branches on `ok` concludes the run succeeded; an agent
that branches on the exit code concludes it failed. Both are reading the same
envelope.

This compounds. A suite whose scorer name does not resolve produces one errored
case at exit 0 with `ok: true` today, and adding `--fail-on-fail` changes the
exit without ever populating `errors`.

Half two, F22. Exit 2 is published as "safety block":

    $ evalctl capabilities --json | jq '.data.exit_codes["2"]'
    {"meaning": "safety block", "retryable": false}

Zero of the 33 registered error codes map to exit 2, and zero of the fifteen
verbs declare it. Nothing in the tool can emit it. `errors.md` notes that a
Codex-style consumer keys denial on exit 2; evalctl publishes a denial channel
that cannot carry a denial.

The two must be decided together. Deciding them apart risks two incompatible
answers about the same dictionary.
design:
Decide, then implement, in that order.

F2 has two coherent answers and they are not equivalent. Either exit 6 means a
completed run with failing cases, which is not a tool failure, in which case
`ok` stays true and the fix is that the exit code alone must never be the only
signal -- the envelope needs a field an agent can branch on, and stderr needs
a line. Or exit 6 is a failure, in which case `ok` becomes false and `errors`
carries a code. The first reading is probably right for an eval harness, since
failing cases are the product, not a malfunction. Pick one and write it into
`capabilities` and the CHANGELOG.

F22 also has two answers. Either exit 2 gets a real emitter, which is the
unsandboxed-runner gate and makes this bead and the runner-safety bead one
fix; or exit 2 leaves the published dictionary and the docs say plainly that
evalctl has no safety block.

The doctor exit-code question tracked separately is the same conversation and
should be folded in or closed into this bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- A written decision on what exit 6 means, recorded in `capabilities` and the CHANGELOG, not only in code.
- Under the chosen reading, `run --fail-on-fail` on a suite with a failing case produces a signal an agent can branch on without reading the exit code, and a line on stderr.
- `ok`, `errors` and the exit code agree with each other under every outcome of `run`, asserted by tests over the full outcome matrix: all pass, some fail, some error, and the runner absent.
- Either exit 2 is reachable and at least one error code declares it, or exit 2 is removed from the published dictionary and from the help text.
- `capabilities.exit_codes` and the set of exits any verb can actually produce are checked against each other by a test, so a dead code cannot be published again.
- The separately tracked doctor exit-code question is resolved or explicitly folded into this bead.
close_reason:
Fixed in commits bb99770 (exit 2 + exit 6), ec71bd4 (dictionary guard test); released as 0.4.4.

F22 (exit 2): exit 2 now has a real emitter, E_UNSANDBOXED_RUNNER_UNACK (class
safety), shared with the runner-safety bead ikb. A new guard test reconciles the
published exit_codes dictionary with the union of exits all verbs declare, both
directions, so a dead code cannot be published again.

F2 (exit 6): chosen reading -- a completed run with failing cases is the product,
not a tool malfunction -- so ok stays true and errors[] stays empty. The
branchable signal is data.fail_on_fail_triggered (true only with --fail-on-fail
and at least one non-passing case), plus a one-line "eval failure:" stderr
summary. Recorded in CHANGELOG 0.4.4 and the errors/agent-guide docs. Outcome
matrix covered by tests (all pass, some fail) plus existing partial-run and
runner-absent tests.

One acceptance criterion is deferred, not met: "the doctor exit-code question is
resolved or explicitly folded." That question remains tracked separately as the
open bead evalctl-1cx; it is not folded here. Left to the user to decide whether
to close 1cx.

title: Fix spoolctl capability probe
description: Evalctl advertises optional queued execution through spoolctl, but the probe path currently assumes a simplified capabilities shape that differs from real spoolctl output. The implementation should make real spoolctl envelope metadata available to the probe, normalize supported add flags from either string entries or structured objects, and distinguish soft capability discovery failures from hard queued-run failures.

title: Add spoolctl JSON runner helper

title: Normalize spoolctl probe parsing
description: The spoolctl capabilities probe currently reads version fields only from unwrapped data and assumes add flags are plain strings. Real spoolctl uses top-level envelope tool_version and structured flag objects, so evalctl must normalize the real shape while retaining compatibility with the older compact string-flag shape.
design:
Update probe_spoolctl() to call the envelope-preserving helper from the previous task. Use the existing envelope discriminator: isinstance(payload, dict) and "ok" in payload. For envelope payloads, require ok:true and object data. Decide explicitly whether non-envelope raw object capabilities output should remain supported; if it remains supported, add a test for that path, otherwise reject it as E_SPOOLCTL_INCOMPATIBLE.

Extract the version from envelope-level tool_version first, then data-level tool_version, then data-level version. Treat envelope-level tool_version as authoritative when present, including when reporting integration version through capabilities_data(). Extract contract_version from capabilities data.

Add a small normalizer such as spoolctl_flag_names(flags) that accepts a list of strings or a list of objects with string "flag" fields and returns a set of flag names. Unknown entries should be ignored, so malformed flags degrade to missing required flags rather than crashing. Keep the required probe criteria: version >= 0.4.1, contract_version == "1", and add flags include --cwd, --env, and --max-crashes.

title: Make status and report see a run that is still in flight
description:
Closes finding F1 of the v0.4.3 make-cli conformance sweep.

This is the archetype's named risk for a build/task orchestrator: reporting on
a plan while the run has not finished.

While a run is executing, observed from a second process:

    jobs get <run-id>     state: running, cases.pending: 2, live reservation
    status <run-id>       E_RUN_NOT_FOUND, exit 1
    report <run-id>       E_RUN_NOT_FOUND, exit 1

`evals/runs/<run-id>/run.json` exists on disk at that moment. Listing the run
directory during the run shows `cases`, `run.json` and `suite-snapshot`, and no
`manifest.json` -- the manifest is written at finalize, and `status` and
`report` appear to key on it.

Three costs, each independent. The verb described as "diagnose run state"
cannot see the only state worth diagnosing. Two verbs reading the same ledger
give contradictory answers about whether a run exists. And the error is wrong
about the world: the run does exist, so an agent told `E_RUN_NOT_FOUND` will
conclude it used the wrong id and go looking for a different one.
design:
`status` and `report` should read the same run-state source `jobs get` reads,
rather than keying on `manifest.json`.

An in-flight run is not an error condition and should not be reported as one.
`status` should report the run's live state with the per-case progress it
already has on disk. `report` is the harder call, since a report over an
unfinished run is a partial artifact: either it reports the finished cases and
marks the report partial in `meta`, or it returns a distinct, correct error
that says the run is still running and offers `evalctl status <id>` as the
command to use instead -- which is a valid answer as long as it is not
`E_RUN_NOT_FOUND`.

Whichever is chosen, the invariant is that no two verbs disagree about whether
a run exists.
acceptance_criteria:
- With a run in flight, `status <run-id>` returns exit 0 and reports the run's live state and per-case progress.
- With a run in flight, `report <run-id>` either returns a partial report flagged in `meta`, or returns an error that names the in-flight state and is not `E_RUN_NOT_FOUND`.
- `jobs get`, `status` and `report` never disagree about whether a given run id exists. Asserted by a test that probes all three against an in-flight run.
- A regression test starts a run long enough to be observed mid-flight and asserts all three verbs from a second process.
- `E_RUN_NOT_FOUND` is returned only for ids that genuinely have no run directory.
close_reason: status now resolves runs like jobs get (dir exists), returns exit 0 with live state + per-case progress mid-flight; report raises new E_RUN_IN_FLIGHT (transient/exit 4) instead of E_RUN_NOT_FOUND. E_RUN_NOT_FOUND reserved for absent run dirs. Regression test asserts jobs get/status/report agree on an in-flight run. Commit 8860c4e.

title: init --force must report the files it deletes
description:
Closes finding F14 of the v0.4.3 make-cli conformance sweep.

`init --force` deletes files it does not report. The envelope describes what
was created and is silent about what was removed to make room.

A destructive flag that under-reports its own effect is the shape of problem
that is discovered after the fact, by someone who cannot reconstruct what was
there. The fix is small and the flag is already explicitly opt-in, so the
severity is in the reporting, not in the deletion.
design:
Report the removals in the envelope: the paths deleted, or a count plus a
bounded sample when the list is long.

Since the flag is already gated behind `--force`, no new confirmation is
needed. This is about the record the call leaves behind.

Worth checking in the same pass whether any other mutating verb removes
something it does not report.
acceptance_criteria:
- `init --force` over an existing tree reports every path it deleted, or a count with a bounded sample.
- The report is in `data`, in a field an agent can branch on.
- A test creates a populated tree, runs `init --force`, and asserts the reported deletions match the filesystem difference exactly.
- `init` without `--force` still refuses rather than deleting.
- No other mutating verb removes a file it does not report. Checked and stated, whether or not it turns up anything.
close_reason: init --force now reports deleted files (commit b12a7f4): data.removed bounded sample + removed_count + removed_truncated; plain init reports empty and still refuses via E_RUN_CONFLICT. Swept jobs prune (already precise) and replay --force (reports the named run_id). Closes F14.

The emitted element/attribute set is FROZEN for the format: JUnit XML has no single
standard and no universal rule that readers ignore an added un-namespaced element, so

ships ZERO extensions. Byte identity is not promised (timestamps/durations vary); the
frozen structure is.

title: report --format junit output-mode rule and matrix
description:
Today `wants_json` is true whenever stdout is not a tty (`commands.py` around line 103:
`json_mode = "--json" in argv or not sys.stdout.isatty()`), so `report RUN --format junit
> out.xml` would arrive in JSON mode and emit a JSON envelope instead of XML. `--format
junit` must force raw XML to stdout regardless of tty state, and `--json` combined with
`--format junit` must be rejected (XML cannot be wrapped in the JSON envelope).
design:
Implement the full output-mode matrix, verified against `commands.py:103,1255-1256`
(explicit `--format markdown` without `--json` prints raw even when piped):
(a) no `--format`, tty -> raw markdown; (b) no `--format`, pipe -> json envelope;
(c) `--format markdown` (any stream, no `--json`) -> raw markdown; (d) `--format json`
-> json envelope; (e) `--format junit` (no `--json`) -> raw XML on success; (f) `--format
markdown|json` plus `--json` -> json envelope; (g) `--format junit` plus `--json` ->
`E_CASE_INVALID`/1. `junit` only joins the raw-output set; every existing behavior is
unchanged.
acceptance_criteria:
- One test per matrix row (a)-(g), including a golden for the rejected `--json --format junit` (row g).
- `report RUN --format junit` emits raw XML in terminal, pipe, and redirection modes.

title: report_formats capability discovery field
description:
A machine client cannot currently learn that `junit` exists — `capabilities` lists flag
NAMES only, and `schema report` describes report DATA, not inputs. Add a named optional
field `report_formats` on the existing `report` capability entry so a client can predict
output rather than reading an undescribed object. This is an additive capability field
(a contract MINOR).
design:
Add `report_formats` on the `report` capability entry with this exact shape (all seven
keys required):
```
"report_formats": {
  "formats": ["markdown", "json", "junit"],
  "default_terminal": "markdown",
  "default_non_terminal": "json",
  "raw_output_formats": ["markdown", "junit"],
  "envelope_formats": ["json"],
  "pagination_policy": {
    "markdown_raw": "ignored",
    "markdown_envelope": "applied",
    "json": "applied",
    "junit": "reject"
  },
  "json_flag_policy": { "markdown": "envelope", "json": "envelope", "junit": "reject" }
}
```
`raw_output_formats` + `envelope_formats` partition `formats`. `pagination_policy` is
two-dimensional on purpose: raw markdown prints the full report and returns BEFORE
`paginate_cases` (`commands.py:1256-1258` vs 1263), so `--limit`/`--cursor` parse but
have no effect (`markdown_raw: ignored`); only markdown inside a `--json` envelope
paginates. Publish these exact properties/types/required-keys in the `schema
capabilities` schema (which currently allows arbitrary objects under `verbs`), and add
the fully-populated object to BOTH the `capabilities` golden and the `schema
capabilities` golden.
acceptance_criteria:

title: Frozen JUnit XML mapping, dialect, and byte encoding
description:
The emitted document must be fixed to an exact, frozen element/attribute set targeting
the Jenkins/surefire-style `<testsuites>`/`<testsuite>`/`<testcase>` schema. Anything
outside the set is a format change, not an additive edit. Ordering, time unit, scorer
identity, one-child precedence, and byte encoding must all be deterministic.
design:
Frozen mapping (value sources cite the case manifest entry and `runner.json`):
- `<testsuites>`/`<testsuite>`: `name` = suite name; `tests` = case count; `failures` =
  cases with status `fail`; `errors` = cases with status `error`; `time` = sum of case
  `duration_ms`/1000, 3 decimals. NO `skipped` attribute (only pass/fail/error status
  exists in 1.1); the frozen-set golden asserts its absence.
- `<testcase>`: `name` = case `id`; `classname` = suite name; `time` = case
  `duration_ms`/1000 (`runner.py:182`), 3 decimals, fixed-point, never scientific.
- `<failure>`: `type` = fixed literal `scorer-failure`; `message` = fixed literal
  `scorer failure; see body`.
- `<error>`: `type` = fixed literal chosen by error-source precedence (`runner-error`
  when `runner.json` timed out or spawn-failed, else `scorer-error`); `message` = fixed
  literal `case errored; see body`. Attributes are constant strings (no derived/secret text).
- Scorer identity in XML: `builtin:<name>` or `command:<id>` (built-in results carry a
  `scorer` name and no `id`; synthesize `builtin:<name>`, never guess a fallback id).
- One child per case by precedence: status `error` -> single `<error>`; else `fail` ->
  single `<failure>`; passed case -> neither. (Status already computed at
  `runner.py:202-208`.)
- Testcase order: byte-wise canonical case-`id` order under `os.fsencode` — the same sort
  `report` uses (`reports.py:31`) — regardless of manifest/input-file order. Root counts
  cover this same complete ordered set.
- Byte encoding: document begins with fixed `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>` + one
  `\n`; write the document as UTF-8 bytes to stdout (encode explicitly, do not rely on
  locale/text-mode encoding of `sys.stdout`). LF line endings throughout; no CRLF, no BOM.
- Ship a golden normative example (pass + multi-fail + mixed fail/error case) as the
  frozen reference.
acceptance_criteria:
- Well-formedness + exact element/attribute mapping goldens for a pass/fail/error run, plus a golden asserting nothing outside the frozen set (incl. the normative multi-fail/mixed example).
- `<testsuites>`/`<testsuite>` emit no `skipped` attribute.
- A deliberately shuffled manifest still yields id-sorted `<testcase>`s.
- A case body with non-ASCII text and a sanitizer `U+FFFD`: the emitted document starts with the UTF-8 declaration, a standard parser reading the RAW emitted bytes accepts it and round-trips the characters; LF endings, no BOM.
notes: 2026-09-03 CLOSED: Added the frozen JUnit document structure with fixed root, suite, testcase, failure, and error attributes. Cases use byte-wise id order and durations use fixed three-decimal seconds. The body pipeline remains isolated for its dependent task. See close reason for commit reference.

title: JUnit bounded, redacted failure-body pipeline and fragment algorithm
description:
The `<failure>`/`<error>` body must contain only marker-approved, capture-redacted text,
built deterministically so two implementations emit identical bodies. Redaction is the
capture-time boundary (the 1.0 cut); JUnit never redacts at report time. The body must
be key-free (a secret can hide in a findings key, which redaction preserves), bounded to
a CI-appropriate size, and XML-valid.
design:
One fixed ordered report-time pipeline per body, five operations in this order, run ONCE
on the whole concatenated body (never per fragment): (1) SELECT the approved key-free
field values as raw fragments (algorithm below); (2) CONCATENATE all of a case's
fragments with a single exact `\n` separator; (3) SANITIZE XML-1.0-illegal characters,
REPLACING each character outside XML-1.0 `Char` with `U+FFFD` (keep `\t \n \r`,
`U+0020..U+D7FF`, `U+E000..U+FFFD`, `U+10000..U+10FFFF`; nothing dropped — replacement
keeps offsets stable); (4) CAP the logical UTF-8 text at 8192 bytes on a codepoint
boundary, truncation-marker bytes (`\n[evalctl: truncated, see run artifacts]`) reserved
FIRST (cap = 8192 - len(marker)); (5) XML-ESCAPE `& < > " '`. Cap before escape so a byte
cap can never split `&`. The 8192 cap bounds LOGICAL diagnostic text, not serialized
XML — do NOT add a second cap on escaped output.

Fragment = one exact join: build an ordered list of item strings, join with exactly one
`\n` between adjacent items (no leading/trailing `\n`).
- Command scorers: item 1 = redacted `label` iff present non-empty after redaction (else
  no item); then each redacted `findings` string LEAF value, one item per leaf, in
  pre-order depth-first order — at each object visit keys in byte-wise (`os.fsencode`)
  order, at each array visit elements in given order; ONLY string leaf values are items,
  keys never, non-string scalars never, empty-string leaves skipped; last item = a tail
  of this scorer's own redacted `cases/<id>/scorers/<scorer-id>.stderr.txt` (NOT
  `runner.stderr.txt`), included iff that file exists, is non-empty, and its verdict
  carries the protocol marker.
- Built-in scorers: exactly two items — `builtin:<name>` and the fixed generic reason
  `built-in scorer <name> failed; see run artifacts` — joined by one `\n`. Built-in
  finding values/why are NEVER emitted (contains/regex put case-expectation strings into
  finding values, `scoring.py:227,234`).
- Runner error: item 1 = fixed reason `runner: <reason>` where `<reason>` is `runner timed
  out` or `runner failed to start` (never `str(exc)`), always present; last item = tail of
  the case's redacted `runner.stderr.txt` (`runner.py:180`) iff it exists, is non-empty,
  and its `runner.json` carries the protocol marker.

Error-source precedence when a case is `error`: runner error first (if `runner.json`
`timed_out` or `spawn_failed`) -> `type=runner-error`, runner fragment is the whole body,
no scorer fragment; else scorer error -> `type=scorer-error`, one fragment per errored
scorer in canonical order (built-ins by name, then command scorers by `id`). A `<failure>`
body concatenates one fragment per failed scorer in that same canonical order. Never
serialize a findings object or emit any object key.
acceptance_criteria:
- A secret in a nested `findings` key and in a value of a COMMAND scorer: JUnit output contains NEITHER (key never emitted, value redacted).
- A built-in `contains`/`regex` finding whose expectation is a secret: JUnit emits only `builtin:<name>` + generic reason, none of the expectation text. Body is exactly `builtin:<name>\nbuilt-in scorer <name> failed; see run artifacts`.
- Error-source precedence (six fixtures): scorer-only -> single `<error type="scorer-error">` with fragments in frozen order; runner-only timeout -> `runner-error`, body `runner: runner timed out` + marker-bearing stderr tail; spawn-fail -> `runner: runner failed to start`; mixed runner+scorer error -> runner precedence, runner fragment only; marker-free runner error -> fixed runner fragment, no stderr tail; missing runner stderr -> fixed runner fragment alone, body never empty.
- Character sanitizer + cap order: a NUL, a lone `U+0001`, a multi-byte char straddling the cap, and a `&`/`<`/`"` exactly on the cap boundary all yield well-formed XML; illegal chars -> `U+FFFD`; no split entity; marker bytes reserved before the cap.
- One body cap across fragments: a case with two near-limit command fragments has exactly ONE 8192-byte cap and ONE truncation marker; escape computed on the concatenated body.
notes: 2026-09-03 CLOSED: Added deterministic key-free JUnit fragments for command scorers, built-in scorers, and runner errors. The body pipeline concatenates once, sanitizes XML 1.0 characters, caps logical UTF-8 text once, then escapes XML. See close reason for commit reference.
close_reason: Added bounded key-free JUnit diagnostic body pipeline — commit ae3503c

title: JUnit protocol-marker legacy gate (per-fragment)
description:
"Old dirs remain reportable" and "JUnit reads only capture-redacted artifacts" conflict
for a pre-1.0 run: its verdicts were never redacted and its env secrets are gone, so
JUnit cannot make them safe at report time. An absent `redacted` field is not proof of
safety. The gate must be per-fragment (per-artifact marker), not per-testcase, so a
testcase with one marker-free and one marker-bearing command scorer stays well-formed and
still surfaces the safe fragment.
design:
Gate on `diagnostics_redaction_version` at FRAGMENT scope. For each selected command
scorer whose verdict LACKS the marker, emit one fixed generic legacy fragment in that
scorer's canonical position: `command:<id>: diagnostic artifact does not prove redaction
protocol v1; diagnostic text omitted (see run artifacts)` — and never emit that scorer's
`label`, `findings`, stdout, stderr, exception text, or any serialized object.
Marker-bearing command scorers keep their redacted fragment; built-in scorers keep their
fixed `builtin:<name>` + generic-reason fragment (built-ins have no verdict and are never
"legacy"); the runner keeps its fixed-reason fragment (constant reason carries no secret),
with only its stderr tail marker-gated by its OWN `runner.json` marker. A mixed
failed/errored testcase emits, in canonical order, the legacy generic fragment for each
marker-free command scorer beside the redacted fragment for each marker-bearing one —
never one generic body swallowing the testcase. The testcase always keeps its correct
status and counts. Covers every case-directory read path: `report --format junit`,
`report --run-dir PATH`, a copied directory with no source workspace, any derived result.
`report --format json/markdown` behavior is unchanged.
acceptance_criteria:
- A pre-1.0 fixture (secret in a scorer verdict, a synthetic `runner.stderr.txt`, and a normal timeout/spawn `runner.stderr.txt`, copied to a fresh dir): JUnit emits the fixed generic legacy fragment for each marker-free command scorer (runner keeps its fixed-reason fragment, no stderr tail) and contains NONE of the secret. The same test on a new marker-bearing normal-runner-failure run shows its redacted stderr tail — proving the rule turns on the marker, not the run.
- A new clean artifact and a new changed artifact both carry `diagnostics_redaction_version: 1` (on `runner.json` and verdict); only the changed one carries `redacted`/`stderr_redacted: true`.
- Mixed-marker legacy testcase (two failed command scorers, one marker-free, one marker-bearing): the `<failure>` body emits, in canonical `command:<id>` order, the legacy fragment beside the marker-bearing redacted fragment; the legacy scorer's `label`/`findings`/stderr never appear; status and counts correct.
notes: Verified the per-fragment protocol marker gate. New tests prove mixed command fragments and runner stderr never expose legacy diagnostic text.
close_reason: Implemented and tested in commit 6ac5cab

title: JUnit error contract and pagination/json rejection
description:
`report --format junit` must print raw XML to stdout ONLY on a successful report. Every
failure to produce a report must use the standard error surface and never emit XML. A
JUnit report is a complete CI test report, so `--limit`/`--cursor` (which would make the
root `tests`/`failures`/`errors` counts lie) must be rejected.
design:
On success, print raw XML. Every produce-failure — missing/unresolvable run
(`E_RUN_NOT_FOUND`/1), run in flight (`E_RUN_IN_FLIGHT`/4), invalid/unreadable artifact
(`E_SCHEMA_VIOLATION`/1) — uses the standard error surface (JSON `errors[]` when
`--json`/non-terminal, human line to stderr otherwise) and a nonzero exit, exactly like
every other verb; it never emits XML and never switches an error to XML based on stdout
being a pipe. `--json` + `--format junit` -> `E_CASE_INVALID`/1. `--format junit` with
either `--limit` or `--cursor` -> `E_CASE_INVALID`/1 on the standard error surface before
any XML. State the rule in `report_formats` (`pagination_policy.junit: "reject"`), its
`schema capabilities` descriptor, and `report --help` — NOT in `schema report` (which
describes output, not inputs).
acceptance_criteria:
- A piped `E_RUN_NOT_FOUND` and a terminal one both take the standard error surface (never XML); a successful piped report emits XML.
- `--json --format junit` -> `E_CASE_INVALID`; `--format junit --limit 1` -> `E_CASE_INVALID`; separately `--format junit --cursor <c>` -> `E_CASE_INVALID` (both rejected flags tested).
notes: Reopened after review. Piped JUnit failures now use the normal JSON error envelope, while successful reports still write raw XML.
close_reason: Verified and corrected in commit d6fef0f

title: Surface redaction metadata in report json/markdown
description:
When capture-time redaction changed a value, a reader of `report --format json/markdown`
should know the displayed diagnostic text was altered. Today `report_score` drops the
verdict's `redacted` flag (`reports.py:38-42`). The JUnit XML deliberately carries NO
redaction marker (the frozen table has none, and a redaction can occur in a leaf JUnit
never selects), so this signal lives only in the JSON/markdown report and the artifacts.
design:
Add two OPTIONAL report-JSON fields, present only when true (absent, not false, otherwise
— keeping the projection additive for old readers): a per-score `redacted: true` on each
score object in `report_score` (stop dropping the verdict's `redacted`), and a per-case
`runner_stderr_redacted: true` read from that case's `runner.json` `stderr_redacted`.
Markdown appends a trailing `(redacted)` marker on a redacted score line and a case-level
`runner stderr redacted` note (the token `(redacted)` is stable wording). The
`diagnostics_redaction_version` marker is NOT surfaced in report output — it is an
artifact-integrity field for the JUnit gate only. Add both fields to the report JSON schema.
acceptance_criteria:
- A redacted score and a redacted runner stderr each assert the corresponding field in `report --format json`.
- Markdown shows the `(redacted)` marker and the case-level note.
- Both fields are absent (not false) when no redaction occurred.
notes: Added optional report JSON redaction fields, Markdown markers, and schema coverage. The fields are present only when capture redaction changed data.
