title: Fix spoolctl contract-version floor
description:
`evalctl run <suite> --queue spoolctl` fails with `E_SPOOLCTL_INCOMPATIBLE`
(exit 3) against every spoolctl release that can currently be installed. The
entire queued execution path is unusable.

The compatibility probe in `evalctl/spoolctl.py` requires spoolctl's
`contract_version` to equal `"1"` exactly. spoolctl bumped `CONTRACT_VERSION`
to `2` in its 0.4.5 release, so every release from 0.4.5 onward is rejected.
Verified by running both binaries together: patching only that equality check
makes the full queued path work end to end, so the gate is the sole blocker.

An equality pin on a sibling tool's contract turns each of that tool's routine
releases into an evalctl outage. The same failure recurs at contract 3 unless
the comparison becomes a floor.

Two related defects travel with it. The advertised minimum, `spoolctl >= 0.4.1`,
names a version that was never published to PyPI (only `0.1.0a1` and `0.4.11`
exist), so every hint tells users to install something unobtainable. And a
single generic message covers three unrelated causes — old version, old
contract, missing flags — while `evalctl doctor` detects the problem and then
recommends re-running `evalctl doctor`.
acceptance_criteria:
- Queued runs succeed against real spoolctl 0.4.11 speaking contract 2.
- A spoolctl reporting a contract newer than the floor (10, 17) is accepted.
- Version, contract, and missing-flag mismatches produce three distinguishable
  errors, each carrying machine-readable fields.
- Every hint names a version installable by the command it prints.
- `evalctl doctor` never recommends running `evalctl doctor`.
- Absent spoolctl remains soft degradation; the standalone synchronous path is
  unaffected.
- evalctl's own `contract_version` stays `1` and report hashes stay compatible
  with v0.4 for comparable runs.
- `evalctl doctor` exit codes are unchanged by this work.
- `pyproject.toml` version is unchanged by this work.
- Full unittest suite passes both with and without spoolctl installed.

The gate reports three distinguishable causes (version / contract / missing add flags), each with machine-readable fields, keeping E_SPOOLCTL_INCOMPATIBLE and exit 3. Prerelease versions at the floor are rejected. capabilities reports minimum_version, minimum_contract, and the observed contract_version. doctor recommends an installable fix instead of re-running itself; doctor exit codes unchanged. evalctl's own contract_version stays 1 and pyproject.toml was not touched. Absent spoolctl remains soft degradation, proven in both configurations. Validated end to end against real spoolctl 0.4.11 with report-hash parity to pre-change main. title: Add integration contracts module with spoolctl floors
description:
The supported spoolctl version is hard-coded as the literal `0.4.1` in at least
five places: the compatibility gate, three error hints, the `capabilities`
integrations block, and the robot-docs prose. Scattered literals are the
mechanism by which the advertised minimum went stale while the gate said
something different.

A single home for integration policy prevents the next drift.
design:
Add `evalctl/integration_contracts.py` holding `MINIMUM_SPOOLCTL_VERSION`
("0.4.11"), `MINIMUM_SPOOLCTL_CONTRACT` (2), and one shared upgrade hint string.

Deliberately a new module rather than `static_contract.py`: that module is
evalctl's own machine-contract surface, and mixing runtime integration policy
into it means a future hint-string tweak drags the static contract and its
golden files along. Both `spoolctl.py` and `static_contract.py` import from the
new module, which also avoids a circular import (`spoolctl.py` already imports
`static_contract`).

Stdlib only. This work adds no runtime dependency.

- `evalctl/integration_contracts.py` exists with the two floor constants and one
  shared hint string.
- No `0.4.1` literal remains in `evalctl/` as a spoolctl minimum.
- Both `spoolctl.py` and `static_contract.py` source the values from the new
  module.
- No import cycle; full suite still passes.

title: Parse spoolctl contract version numerically
description:
The probe reads spoolctl's contract version as a string. Replacing the broken
equality check with a string comparison such as `contract >= "2"` would sort
`"10"` before `"2"` and recreate the same forward-compatibility failure one
spoolctl release later — the exact bug class this work exists to remove.

The comparison must be numeric.
design:
Add a parser converting the observed contract to `int`. Accept integer `2` and
string `"2"` — spoolctl's JSON type for this field is not guaranteed. Reject
missing, empty, non-numeric, and non-positive values as
`E_SPOOLCTL_INCOMPATIBLE` (exit 3, unchanged).

Malformed values raise with the same `observed_contract` and `minimum_contract`
fields as the below-floor case, so consumers see one error shape per cause
rather than one shape for old-but-valid values and another for garbage.
acceptance_criteria:
- Integer `2` and string `"2"` both parse and are accepted.
- Contract `"10"` is accepted, proving the compare is numeric not lexicographic.
- Missing, empty, non-numeric, and non-positive contracts raise
  `E_SPOOLCTL_INCOMPATIBLE`, never a traceback.
- Every rejection carries `observed_contract` and `minimum_contract`.
close_reason: Added parse_spoolctl_contract() in evalctl/spoolctl.py. Accepts int 2 and str "2"; contract 10 and 17 parse above 2, proving the compare is numeric not lexicographic. Missing, empty, non-numeric, non-positive, bool, and non-scalar values raise E_SPOOLCTL_INCOMPATIBLE (exit 3) with observed_contract and minimum_contract, never a traceback; error dicts asserted JSON-serializable. Two unit tests added. Parser is deliberately not wired into the gate here - that is evalctl-npw.4. Suite 78 tests, OK, 2 skipped. Commit 06f48f9.

title: Reject prerelease spoolctl versions below the floor
description:
The existing `version_tuple` helper takes the numeric prefix of each
dot-segment and discards the rest. Verified behavior: `0.4.11-rc1`,
`0.4.11rc1`, `0.4.11.dev1`, and `0.4.11+local` all map to `(0, 4, 11)`, so a
release candidate of the floor release passes as though it were the final
release.

That is the same class of sloppiness as the contract equality check — a version
comparison that quietly does the wrong thing. Leaving it implicit inside the
work that fixes that class is not defensible, so the policy is chosen and
pinned rather than inherited by accident.
design:
Policy:

    Accept final versions >= 0.4.11.
    Reject prerelease-like versions whose base version is not above 0.4.11.
    Accept local/build metadata when the base final version is >= 0.4.11.

So `0.4.11rc1` is rejected (base equals the floor, and an rc precedes its
final); `0.4.12rc1` and `0.5.0a1` are accepted (base above the floor);
`0.4.11+local` is accepted.

Small local parser with its own tests. No `packaging` dependency — evalctl is
stdlib-only and this work does not change that.

Keep the parser small on purpose. The version floor is a proxy; the contract
floor and the `add`-flag check are the substantive capability gates, and a

title: Split spoolctl compatibility gate into three checks
description:
One boolean expression currently decides three unrelated questions — is the
version new enough, is the contract the right one, are the required `add` flags
present — and raises a single message, "spoolctl is missing required evalctl
queue capabilities", for all of them. A user whose spoolctl is merely a
contract version ahead is told flags are missing.

The contract half of that expression is also the outage: it tests equality
where it must test a floor.
design:
Replace the single expression with three checks, each raising
`E_SPOOLCTL_INCOMPATIBLE` (error code and exit code 3 both unchanged, so this
is not a contract change) and each carrying its own machine-readable fields:

    version below floor / prerelease of floor -> observed_version, minimum_version
    contract below floor / missing / malformed -> observed_contract, minimum_contract
    missing add flags                          -> missing_flags (sorted list)

The contract check compares `>=` against the floor constant, never equality.
A comment must record why, naming this incident: the equality form looks more
careful and will otherwise be "corrected" back by a future reader.

Newer-than-floor contracts are accepted with no upper bound. There is
deliberately no maximum-tested constant, and therefore no newer-contract
warning and no degraded state — without such a constant "newer than tested"
cannot be computed, and a constant that must be bumped on every spoolctl
release will go stale.
acceptance_criteria:
- Three distinct failure messages, one per cause, each with its fields.
- Contract 2 accepted; contracts 10 and 17 accepted.
- Contract 1 rejected with observed and minimum contract reported.
- Version below the floor rejected with observed and minimum version reported.
- A missing required `add` flag is rejected and named in `missing_flags`.
- `E_SPOOLCTL_INCOMPATIBLE` and exit 3 are unchanged.
close_reason: probe_spoolctl() now runs three separate checks, each raising E_SPOOLCTL_INCOMPATIBLE (exit 3, unchanged) with its own fields: version -> observed_version/minimum_version, contract -> observed_contract/minimum_contract, flags -> missing_flags (sorted). Contract compares >= MINIMUM_SPOOLCTL_CONTRACT, never equality, with a comment naming this incident so a future reader does not 'correct' it back. No maximum-tested constant, so no upper bound and no newer-contract warning. Test asserts three distinct messages and their fields; contract 1 rejected, version below floor rejected, missing --max-crashes named. Landed with evalctl-npw.5 in one commit because raising the contract floor alone fails every fake-fixture queued-run test. Suite 81 tests, OK, 2 skipped. Commit 6cd5cf0.

- Existing queued-run tests pass without per-test version overrides.
- Rejection tests pass old values explicitly.

title: Add forward-compatibility regressions for newer contracts
description:
The defect being fixed is a forward-compatibility bug: evalctl rejected a
spoolctl contract newer than the one it was written against. A test suite that
only pins today's contract value would reproduce the same outage one spoolctl
release from now and call it passing.

The regression that matters is not "contract 2 works" but "a contract we have
never seen works".
design:
Drive the probe with contracts 2, 10, and 17 and assert all are accepted.
Contract 10 does double duty: it also proves the comparison is numeric rather
than lexicographic, since `"10" < "2"` as strings.

Add a comment recording why the test exists, so a future reader does not
simplify it back to a single current-value assertion.
acceptance_criteria:
- Contracts 2, 10, and 17 are all accepted by the probe.
- A test comment records the forward-compatibility rationale.
- Tests fail if the gate is reverted to an equality check.

Test comment records the forward-compatibility rationale so it is not simplified to a single current-value assertion. Verified the test fails when the gate is reverted to equality (3 of 5 subtests fail), then restored the file. Suite 82 tests, OK, 2 skipped. Commit 59e1151.

title: Report spoolctl contract version in capabilities
description:
The `capabilities` integrations block reports only a spoolctl version and a
minimum version. Version alone cannot diagnose a contract mismatch, which is
precisely the failure this work fixes — a user reporting "queued runs are
broken" gives no way to see which contract their spoolctl speaks or which one
evalctl wants.
design:
When spoolctl is available, the integrations block reports:

    {"available": true, "planned": false, "minimum_version": "0.4.11",
     "minimum_contract": 2, "version": "0.4.11", "contract_version": 2}

When spoolctl is unavailable or incompatible, behavior stays soft — exit 0,
`available: false` — and the block keeps `minimum_version` and
`minimum_contract`, so a user can see what was required without a working
spoolctl.

Contract fields are integers, consistent with numeric parsing.
acceptance_criteria:
- `minimum_version` and `minimum_contract` are always present.
- Observed `version` and `contract_version` are present when spoolctl is
  available.
- Contract fields are integers.
- Absent spoolctl still exits 0 with `available: false`.

Contract fields are ints, asserted by isinstance. Absent spoolctl still exits 0 with available:false and both minimums present. Capabilities golden re-pinned: diff is the added minimum_contract field plus the data_hash. Suite 83 tests, OK, 2 skipped. Commit a3e0ae8.

title: Fix doctor spoolctl recommendation and pin exit code
description:
`evalctl doctor` correctly detects an unusable spoolctl and reports the
component as `unhealthy`, then recommends running
`evalctl doctor --component spoolctl --fast --json` — that is, running the
diagnosis again. Diagnosing correctly and prescribing a re-run of the diagnosis
is a doctor-quality defect independent of the version gate. The absent-binary
path also recommends installing a version that was never published.

Separately, `evalctl doctor` exits 0 even with a component in `unhealthy`
state. That is a live behavior question worth deciding deliberately later, so
this work pins the current behavior rather than changing it in passing.
design:
The incompatible branch recommends an install command naming the floor version,
with the probe's own message as rationale, plus the alternative of running
without `--queue spoolctl`. The absent-binary branch names the same installable
version. Neither may recommend running `evalctl doctor`.

Report the observed contract version in the component's `observed` block.

Exit codes are explicitly unchanged. Add a test asserting an unhealthy spoolctl
component still exits 0, so that a future decision to change doctor's exit
contract is made deliberately rather than discovered as a regression.
acceptance_criteria:
- Incompatible spoolctl yields a recommendation to install or upgrade, with the
  run-without-queue alternative.
- Absent spoolctl recommends an installable version.
- No doctor recommendation invokes `evalctl doctor`.
- Observed contract version appears in the component's observed block.
- A test pins that an unhealthy component still exits 0.

Observed contract_version and minimum_contract appear in the component's observed block on both healthy and incompatible paths. No spoolctl or inferctl recommendation invokes evalctl doctor; the inferctl branch had the same self-referential defect and now points at 'inferctl capabilities --json'. title: Capture-time recursive redact_json over verdicts and synthetic runner error
description:
The whole command-scorer verdict is stored unredacted via `write_json(verdict_path,
result)` in `evalctl/scoring.py`, and every text-bearing field in it is
attacker-influenced: `label` is an arbitrary caller string, `findings` is a list of
arbitrary nested objects (`scoring.py` normalize path), and `scorer_failure` puts free
text — including decoded scorer stdout fragments — into `findings[].why`. Separately,
the synthetic runner-error path writes `str(exc)` to `runner.stderr.txt` uncapped and
unredacted (`runner.py` around line 63), unlike the normal capture path which is
bounded and redacted. The existing `apply_redaction` is text-only and cannot walk these
nested shapes. This is a secret-leak on exactly the portable run directory the tool
promises, so it is fixed at capture time — a report-time pass cannot be the boundary
because a copied run dir no longer holds the original `os.environ` secrets that
`apply_redaction` resolves against at run time.

This task also lands the three additive artifact fields the fix and the JUnit gate
depend on, and the shape of the synthetic whole-verdict-limit failure artifact.
design:
Add one capture-time function `redact_json(value, patterns, env_values)` in a new
`evalctl/redaction.py` module. Walk the JSON; for EVERY string leaf value — `label`,
each `findings[]` object's every string value at any depth, `scorer_failure` `why`,
and the synthetic runner error string — apply the existing per-leaf cap→redact→cap
order (as in `scoring.py` around 199-204) using the run's `redact_env_values` +
`redact_patterns`. Object keys and non-string scalars (numbers, booleans, null) pass
through unchanged so `ok`/`score`/`required`/`error_code` and verdict shape are
preserved. Run it over the entire command-scorer verdict before `write_json`, and over
the synthetic runner error before it is written (`runner.py:63`).

Additive artifact fields (optional, old readers ignore them):
- `diagnostics_redaction_version: 1` on every new command-scorer verdict AND every new
  `runner.json` (normal and synthetic) — always present, meaning "a redaction-aware
  writer produced this", distinct from whether any value changed.
- `redacted: true` on the verdict when a string value was replaced.
- `stderr_redacted: true` on `runner.json` when that artifact's stderr was replaced.

Synthetic whole-verdict-limit failure artifact shape (produced by the limit paths in
the sibling tasks): written through the same redact_json + cap path, carrying the
version marker, `error_code: E_SCORER_CASE_FAILED`, `verdict_truncated: true` (recorded
separately from `redacted`), and a single fixed safe finding
`{"why": "verdict exceeded <limit-name> limit; see run artifacts"}` that never echoes
oversized content; `<limit-name>` from the fixed enum
`stdout-bytes|depth|node-count|serialized-size`.

Security boundary is string values only: keys are preserved by design, and report
JSON/markdown still serialize whole findings objects (`reports.py:39`), so a secret
hidden in a findings KEY remains a known named residual, not closed here.
acceptance_criteria:
- A scorer whose `label`, nested `findings`, and a synthetic runner error each carry an env value + a pattern match: stored verdict/stderr string values are redacted; non-string fields and verdict shape unchanged.
- `diagnostics_redaction_version: 1` present on every new verdict and on both normal and synthetic `runner.json`; `redacted`/`stderr_redacted` set only when a replacement occurred (marker present != replacement occurred).
- A secret in a nested `findings` KEY is NOT redacted (documented residual); a secret in a `findings` VALUE is redacted.
- An old pre-1.0 run dir still reports byte-identically under json/markdown.
- A non-secret diagnostic leaf longer than the per-leaf cap is shortened but carries NEITHER `redacted` NOR `verdict_truncated` (per-leaf capping is pre-existing and unflagged).

title: Structural verdict bounds enforced at parse time
description:
`run_command_scorer` calls `json.loads(stdout.strip())` (`scoring.py` around line 194)
BEFORE any depth/node check, so a deeply nested or very wide document is fully
materialized — and can overflow the parser's own recursion or exhaust memory — before
any guard runs. Per-leaf redaction does not bound the whole structure: an arbitrary
list of arbitrary nested objects still permits millions of leaves, unbounded depth (a
recursion overflow inside the redactor), and a huge verdict file. Hard structural
limits are needed, enforced during tokenization before graph construction.
design:
Fixed contract constants live in ONE source of truth (`evalctl/redaction.py` module
constants), read by implementations, never re-picked:

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `VERDICT_MAX_STDOUT_BYTES` | resolved `max_output_bytes` (default 5*1024*1024) | raw stdout UTF-8 bytes accepted before `json.loads` |
| `VERDICT_MAX_DEPTH` | 32 | root value is depth 1; reject on entering depth 33 |
| `VERDICT_MAX_NODES` | 10000 | any JSON value is a node; reject on visiting node 10001 |
| `VERDICT_MAX_SERIALIZED_BYTES` | 1048576 | UTF-8 length of the exact `write_json` serialization (indent=2, sort_keys=True, +"\n"), measured after redaction |

Enforce depth, node count, and string validity in a TOKEN validator before graph
construction — `object_pairs_hook` is insufficient (it fires only after an object is
built, and never sees arrays or bare scalars). Use either (a) a streaming/token-level
parser that checks depth before entering each object/array and counts every value, or
(b) a complete token-level validation pass over raw stdout before any `json.loads`.
Never hand an unbounded/unvalidated document to the default recursive parser.
`redact_json` then walks the already-validated graph only for redaction and stored-byte
measurement — it is NOT the depth/node enforcement pass. Ordering matters: with
duplicate keys the `json.loads` graph holds FEWER nodes than the token stream, so a
count taken inside `redact_json` would undercount.

The serialized-size check runs on the actual bytes `write_json` stores (indented,
sorted, newline-terminated — larger than compact `stable_json`), computed once and both
length-checked and stored.

Two rules bind BOTH parser options: reject any JSON string (key or value) that is not a
sequence of Unicode scalar values — a lone UTF-16 surrogate `U+D800..U+DFFF` (which
`json.loads` accepts but `os.fsencode`/UTF-8 encode reject) — as an ordinary
command-scorer parse error (`E_SCORER_CASE_FAILED`, not a structural limit), before
redaction/sort/cap. And duplicate object keys: accept, last value wins (matching
`json.loads`). Simplest conformant design: both options are token validators, then one
shared `json.loads` builds the graph.

Map a lexer/parser resource failure (RecursionError, token depth ceiling) to the
`depth` synthetic verdict; a node-counter ceiling to `node-count`; a plain malformed-JSON
error stays the ordinary scorer parse failure. All limit rejections map to
`E_SCORER_CASE_FAILED` via the synthetic-limit artifact (defined in the redact_json task).
acceptance_criteria:
- Boundary: depth 32 accepts / 33 rejects; 10000 nodes accept / 10001 reject; a verdict whose compact `stable_json` fits but whose stored pretty `write_json` bytes exceed `VERDICT_MAX_SERIALIZED_BYTES` is rejected into the `serialized-size` synthetic verdict.
- A document far beyond `VERDICT_MAX_DEPTH` and one beyond `VERDICT_MAX_NODES` each fail into the correct `depth`/`node-count` synthetic verdict WITHOUT a full `json.loads` of the graph and with no uncaught `RecursionError`.
- A lone surrogate in a findings key and in a findings value each fail into the ordinary parse error before redaction, with no `UnicodeEncodeError` reaching the caller — in both parser options.
- A verdict repeating a `findings`/`label` object key: stored verdict and downstream fragment both use the LAST value, identically under either parser option.

The validator limits depth and nodes, rejects lone surrogates, preserves last-key behavior, and uses the exact stored JSON bytes for the whole-verdict size limit. Tests cover boundaries and safe synthetic artifacts. See close reason for commit reference.

title: Bounded process capture for command scorers
description:
The raw-stdout byte limit cannot be enforced after the fact. `run_process`
(`evalctl/processes.py`) is `text=True` and calls `proc.communicate(...)`, which buffers
the child's entire stdout and stderr in memory before returning; `run_command_scorer`
then parses the full string and only afterwards applies its byte slice. A scorer that
writes gigabytes exhausts memory before any limit runs. A real bounded-capture path is
needed for command scorers.
design:
Scope: a command-scorer-only bounded byte-capture path. Do NOT edit the shared
`run_process` — it is also called by the runner (`runner.py`), and changing it would
silently alter runner behavior. Runner output capture stays as-is and is explicitly NOT
bounded this phase.

Two exact byte terms for a stream with budget B (B = `VERDICT_MAX_STDOUT_BYTES` for
stdout; B = resolved `max_output_bytes` for stderr): AT LIMIT = reader retained exactly
B bytes and the child produced no further byte — accepted, not truncated. OVERFLOW =
reader observed byte B+1. A process writing exactly B bytes is at limit, parsed normally.

Rules:
- Retain at most B bytes per stream; keep reading past B only to detect whether byte B+1
  exists; discard every byte after B (never block the pipe). Decode with UTF-8
  `errors="replace"`.
- Drain both streams CONCURRENTLY (two reader threads or select/event loop) — never
  sequential read of one full stream then the other, which deadlocks when the child
  blocks writing the unread stream.
- Verdict gains two REQUIRED booleans `stdout_capture_truncated` / `stderr_capture_truncated`,
  each true iff that stream reached overflow; old verdicts lacking them read as false.
  Distinct from the runner artifact's `stdout_truncated`/`stderr_truncated`.
- Terminate on STDOUT overflow only, by process group: start the child in a new
  session/process group (`start_new_session=True`, as `run_process` already does). On
  observing stdout byte B+1: (1) latch the `stdout-bytes` result immediately; (2) SIGKILL
  the whole process group at once (`os.killpg(os.getpgid(pid), SIGKILL)`) so a grandchild
  holding an output pipe cannot stall the readers; (3) continue draining both streams for
  at most `kill_drain_timeout` (2.0 s, `processes.py:36`) as a POST-KILL drain bound (not
  a pre-kill grace), discarding past B; (4) reap and return the latched `stdout-bytes`
  synthetic verdict. This kill precedes and overrides the normal command timeout. STDERR
  overflow alone never kills and never changes the verdict — stderr is drained/discarded
  past B, its truncated flag set, and the scorer returns its real verdict.
- Fixed failure precedence: spawn-failure > `stdout-bytes` (overflow) > timeout >
  nonzero-exit. On stdout overflow the scorer does NOT `json.loads` a partial document —
  it fails into the fixed `stdout-bytes` synthetic verdict.
acceptance_criteria:
- A scorer writing far more than `VERDICT_MAX_STDOUT_BYTES` fails into `stdout-bytes`; retained capture <= B (the test process never holds the full output); the child is terminated.
- Stdout exactly at limit (B bytes) parses normally with `stdout_capture_truncated: false`; stdout-only overflow -> `stdout-bytes` with `stdout_capture_truncated: true`; stderr-only overflow -> the real verdict with stderr truncated + `stderr_capture_truncated: true`, child NOT killed; stdout overflow then a slow child -> `stdout-bytes` (killed on overflow, never reaching timeout).
- A scorer that spawns a grandchild keeping stdout open then overflows stdout still terminates and returns `stdout-bytes` within the 2.0 s post-kill drain (group kill reaps the grandchild).
- A child alternating writes larger than the OS pipe buffer to BOTH streams completes within bounded test time (proves concurrent drain; a sequential reader would deadlock).
- Both `*_capture_truncated` fields present and Boolean on every new verdict; read as false when absent from an old verdict.
notes: 2026-09-03 CLOSED: Added command-scorer-only concurrent bounded capture. Stdout overflow terminates the process group and produces a safe synthetic verdict; stderr overflow is retained only as a capture flag. Tests cover exact limits, stream draining, and group cleanup. See close reason for commit reference.

title: Validate max_output_bytes at the validate_suite chokepoint
description:
The output budget B is the resolved `max_output_bytes`, but today it is read with a
Python truth-value fallback — `int(scorer.get("max_output_bytes") or
runner.get("max_output_bytes") or 5*1024*1024)` (`scoring.py` around line 162) — so `0`
silently becomes the 5 MiB default, a negative value is used as-is (breaking the B+1
rule), and a non-integer raises deep in scoring. `validate_suite` checks none of it.
Zero, negative, and non-integer values need a defined preflight result.
design:
Add one validation rule at the shared `validate_suite` chokepoint (`evalctl/suite.py`,
the same preflight the redaction-config check uses): `runner.max_output_bytes` and any
command-scorer `max_output_bytes` override, when present, must be a JSON integer >= 1.
Because Python's `bool` subclasses `int`, use `type(value) is int` (NOT
`isinstance(value, int)`), so a JSON `true`/`false` is rejected, never read as budget
1/0. A missing value takes the 5*1024*1024 default. Resolution order stays scorer
override, then runner, then default — but now over validated integers, so the `or`
fallback can no longer swallow a `0`. A present value that is `0`, negative, a float, a
Boolean, or a non-numeric type is rejected as `E_CASE_INVALID`/exit 1 BEFORE any run
directory is created — same surface and timing as the invalid-redact_patterns rule.
acceptance_criteria:
- A valid scorer override is accepted and used ahead of the runner value.
- `0`, `-1`, `1.5`, `true`, `false`, and `"big"` are each rejected at `validate_suite` as `E_CASE_INVALID`/exit 1 with NO run directory created (`true`/`false` proving `type(value) is int`, not `isinstance`).
notes: 2026-09-03 CLOSED: Added shared validation for runner and command-scorer output budgets. Values must be JSON integers of at least one; scorer overrides preserve precedence. Tests cover invalid values and preflight timing. See close reason for commit reference.

title: Reject invalid redaction config at validate_suite before any case runs
description:
A `redact_patterns` entry that fails `re.compile` is malformed suite config, not a case
failure. It must be rejected before any case executes, on every path that can reach the
redaction code — not just `run`/`plan`. Because `replay` also runs runners and command
scorers (`commands.py` around 1105-1124), skipping it would let a bad regex reach the
redaction code after a new replay run directory exists, defeating the preflight promise.
design:
Add the `re.compile` check at the shared `validate_suite` chokepoint, which every
execution entry point already calls:

| Entry point | Where it validates | Run-dir result on reject |
|---|---|---|
| `validate` | `validate_suite` directly | no run directory |
| `run` / `plan` | preflight `validate_suite` | no run directory |
| `resume` | `validate_suite` on the resumed suite before remaining cases | existing run dir NOT advanced |
| `replay` | `validate_suite(suite_dir)` (`commands.py:1124`) before target cases | reject before any replay case runs |
| queued execution (if independent entry point) | same `validate_suite` gate | no case executes |

Reject as `E_CASE_INVALID`/exit 1 on the envelope surface (user-input error), distinct
from a per-case `E_SCORER_CASE_FAILED`. This keeps "config is wrong" and "a case
errored" on different machine-distinguishable channels.
acceptance_criteria: - An invalid `redact_patterns` regex is rejected at `run` (no run dir) AND at `replay` (existing run dir not advanced), both `E_CASE_INVALID`/exit 1.
notes: 2026-09-03 CLOSED: Added redaction-pattern compilation at shared suite validation. Invalid patterns now fail as configuration errors before run or replay creates a new run directory. Tests cover both entry points. See close reason for commit reference.
close_reason: Validated redaction patterns before run and replay execution — commit 3f746b3

title: Make --help and --json per-verb aware; a read-only probe is a write path
description:
Closes findings F12 and F23 of the v0.4.3 make-cli conformance sweep.

`--help` and `--json` are registered as global flags, so they survive the
unknown-flag rejection added in v0.4.1 and reach verbs that never act on them.
Only the top-level dispatcher acts on `--help`. The consequence is that a verb
runs when the caller asked for its documentation:

    $ evalctl init --help
    (scaffolds evals/suites/code-review and the runs tree, exit 0)

    $ evalctl run code-review --help
    (executes the full eval run, exit 0)

Confirmed in a clean empty directory, then reproduced across `run`, `validate`,
`doctor`, `capabilities` and `jobs list`. `capabilities` lists `--help` as a
valid flag for all fifteen verbs, so an agent reading the contract is told the
probe is safe.

Two things are wrong and they are one fix. Per-verb help does not exist, which
is introspection Layer 1 missing outright. And the read-only probe an agent
reaches for first is, on `init` and `run`, a mutation.

F23 is the same root with a smaller blast radius: `robot-docs guide --json`
returns markdown at exit 0 with empty stderr. `capabilities` is honest and
declares `"json": false` for that verb; the fault is that the flag is accepted
and ignored rather than rejected.

This is the only finding in the sweep rated critical. It should land before any
other conformance fix.
design:
Make the flag registry per-verb aware rather than global-or-nothing.

`--help` should be handled by whichever verb it was given to, printing that
verb's own help and exiting 0 without side effects. Per `introspection.md`,
per-subcommand help is required, not optional.

`--json` should be rejected with `E_UNKNOWN_FLAG` on any verb whose
`capabilities` entry declares `"json": false`. Today `robot-docs` is the only
such verb, so the reject list can be derived from the same table that feeds
`capabilities` rather than maintained separately.

Both changes are input-surface changes, so they need grammar tests through the
real CLI parser, not just handler-level tests.
acceptance_criteria:
- `evalctl <verb> --help` prints help for that verb and exits 0 for all fifteen verbs.
- `evalctl init --help` in an empty directory creates no files. Asserted by listing the directory after the call.
- `evalctl run <suite> --help` executes no cases and writes no run directory.
- Each verb's help carries the same AGENT/AUTOMATION footer convention as the global help.
- `evalctl robot-docs guide --json` returns `E_UNKNOWN_FLAG` with exit 1.
- The reject list for `--json` is derived from the same source as the `capabilities` `json` field, so the two cannot drift.
- Grammar tests exercise `--help` and `--json` through the real parser on every verb, including the mutating ones.
- A golden pins at least one per-verb help output.
close_reason:
Fixed in commit 7553ea9, released in 0.4.3; verified 2026-09-01. All acceptance
criteria met and test-covered:

F12 (--help): per-verb --help/-h prints that verb's own help at exit 0 with no
side effects, for all 15 verbs. init --help creates no files; run <suite> --help
executes no cases and writes no run dir. Each verb's help carries the
AGENT/AUTOMATION footer. Help detection follows the flag grammar (--help as a
dash-tolerant flag value is a value; after -- it is positional). Covered by
test_per_verb_help_exists_and_never_mutates,
test_help_on_a_mutating_verb_leaves_the_project_untouched,
test_help_detection_follows_the_flag_grammar; per-verb help pinned by the
help-run.txt golden.

F23 (--json): robot-docs guide --json is rejected with E_UNKNOWN_FLAG at exit 1.
The reject list is derived from CommandSpec.json -- the same field capabilities
publishes -- so the accepted set cannot drift from the advertised one. Covered by
test_json_flag_is_rejected_on_verbs_that_declare_no_envelope. Documented in
CHANGELOG 0.4.3.

title: plan should not propose work a live reservation would refuse
description:
Closes finding F3 of the v0.4.3 make-cli conformance sweep.

`plan` is the highest-weighted verb for this archetype. It is side-effect-free
and its whole value is that an agent can trust the proposal before committing
to it.

With a live reservation held on a run, `plan` proposes the work anyway and its
payload carries no `blocked_by_external`. The agent pastes the proposed command
and the run is refused. The PLAN shape exists so that the plan and the
execution agree; here they do not.
design:
`plan` already reads run state well enough to plan a resume. It should also
check the reservation state it can already see, and carry the result in the
payload rather than discovering it at run time.

Per the PLAN shape, external blockers belong in the plan as data, not as an
absence. A blocked plan is still a useful plan -- it tells the agent what is in
the way and what to do about it -- so this should mark the affected entries
rather than refusing to plan.
acceptance_criteria:
- With a live reservation on a run, `plan` marks the affected work as blocked and names the reservation as the blocker.
- The payload carries the blocker in a field an agent can branch on, populated only when a blocker exists.
- `commands` offers the action that clears or inspects the blocker, not only the run command that would be refused.
- With no reservation held, the plan is unchanged from today. Asserted by a golden.
- A test holds a reservation, plans, releases it, and plans again, asserting both shapes.
close_reason: plan (fresh --run-id and --resume) now detects a live reservation and carries data.blocked_by_external (only when present) naming the reservation + clears_when + recommended status command; affected cases marked blocked, commands point at the blocker not the refused run. title: Bound jobs list pagination

title: Implement plan command
description: Agents need a side-effect-free PLAN surface that shows which cases would run, which would skip, what execution mode would be used, and which follow-up command should be pasted. evalctl cases are independent, so the plan must be honest about resolved case sets and concurrency without inventing dependency edges.
design:
Add canonical command `evalctl plan <suite> [--jobs N] [--timeout S] [--run-id ID] [--resume ID] [--queue spoolctl] [--slots N] [--inferctl-task TASK] [--json]`. A `run --plan` or `run --dry-run` alias may be added only if cheap and unambiguous; do not overload validation.

Plan must not create run directories, write run state, enqueue spoolctl jobs, execute runners or scorers, or invoke inferctl in a way that persists prompt content. description: Reusing a completed `--run-id` against a different suite or case set currently returns the stale completed run. Agents need completed-run reuse to be idempotent only when the current suite identity matches the stored manifest.
design:
On completed run-id reuse, compare the current suite name, suite hash, and sorted list of `(case_id, input_hash)` pairs against the stored manifest. A match returns the existing run with `existing:true`. A mismatch raises `E_RUN_CONFLICT` with exit 5, names the existing run-id clash, and suggests using a fresh run id. Manifest-less reservation directories remain `E_RUN_BUSY`.

Enrich the idempotent response with `run_id`, `run_dir`, `run{ok,case_count,status_counts}`, `report_hash`, and `existing:true`, using `report_data(run_dir)` where possible. Preserve `W_UNSANDBOXED_RUNNER` on this early-return path.
acceptance_criteria:
- Rerunning the same suite and same run id returns exit 0, `existing:true`, `run_id`, `run_dir`, `run`, `report_hash`, and `W_UNSANDBOXED_RUNNER`.
- Editing a case body and reusing the same run id returns `E_RUN_CONFLICT`, exit 5, and does not overwrite artifacts.
- Renaming a case id with identical content also returns `E_RUN_CONFLICT`, exit 5, and does not overwrite artifacts.
- A manifest-less reservation directory still returns `E_RUN_BUSY`, exit 4.
notes:
COMPLETED:
- Added current/stored run identity comparison using suite name, suite hash, and sorted (case_id, input_hash) pairs.
- Completed-run reuse now returns existing:true with run_id, run_dir, run summary, report_hash, and W_UNSANDBOXED_RUNNER.
- Reuse with edited case content or renamed case id now raises E_RUN_CONFLICT exit 5 without overwriting artifacts.
- Manifest-less reservation directories still return E_RUN_BUSY exit 4.
- Verified with python3 -m unittest discover -s tests.

title: Cap output file bytes
description: `EVALCTL_OUTPUT_FILE` is read without a cap and `runner.json.output_truncated` is always false. This can produce unbounded artifacts and dishonest metadata.
design: Read at most `max_output_bytes` raw bytes from `EVALCTL_OUTPUT_FILE`, then decode with UTF-8 replacement, mirroring stdout/stderr handling. Set `runner.json.output_truncated` truthfully and include output-file truncation in `W_OUTPUT_TRUNCATED`. Truncate before redaction and before writing back to `output.txt` so the persisted artifact and scored text match. Keep scorers text-based on the decoded replacement text; byte-exact scoring is out of scope.
acceptance_criteria:

- The run emits `W_OUTPUT_TRUNCATED`.
- The captured raw bytes are capped at `max_output_bytes`; the persisted decoded file may differ in on-disk byte length for invalid or multibyte input.
- Scoring and report replay use the capped persisted artifact.

title: Skip non-UTF-8 paths

Explicitly reject surrogate code points before any `stable_json(..., ensure_ascii=False)` serialization. Skip such entries and emit `W_PATH_UNREADABLE` with a best-effort lossy path. Preserve existing symlink, FIFO, and hash-error handling.

- The run emits `W_PATH_UNREADABLE` naming the problematic path.
- The run still completes and scores other paths.

title: Add reservation TTL heartbeat
description: An incomplete run directory currently behaves like a permanent reservation. After a process crash, later invocations cannot distinguish a live run from abandoned state.
design: Add a liveness-only `.reservation.json` sidecar containing run id, process diagnostics, start timestamp, heartbeat timestamp, and TTL seconds. Start a background heartbeat during run and resume execution. Use TTL-based liveness for contention: live reservations return `E_RUN_BUSY`; stale reservations are reclaimable only through `run --resume`; plain `run` against stale incomplete state returns `E_RUN_BUSY` with a resume hint. Clear the reservation after successful finalization.
acceptance_criteria:
- `--reservation-ttl` is accepted on `run` and defaults to 3600 seconds.
- A concurrent invocation against a live run returns `E_RUN_BUSY` with exit 4.
- A long-running case stays live because the heartbeat updates independently of case boundaries.
- After TTL expiry, `run --resume <run-id>` reclaims stale state and emits `W_RESERVATION_RECLAIMED`.
- Plain `run --run-id <id>` against a stale incomplete dir returns `E_RUN_BUSY` and does not clobber the run.
- Successful finalization clears the reservation sidecar.

For incomplete runs, require `suite-snapshot/`, valid `run.json`, and a stale or absent reservation. Verify `run.json.suite_identity` matches the suite snapshot. title: Make replay idempotent independently of the wall-clock second
description:
Closes finding F8 of the v0.4.3 make-cli conformance sweep.

`replay`'s idempotency on retry depends on which wall-clock second the retry
lands in: retrying inside the same second behaves differently from retrying
across one.

Determinism is one of the highest-weighted axes for this archetype, and this is
the one place the tool fails it. Everything else checked clean -- nine of nine
non-mutating verbs produce identical bytes across repeated calls,
`SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` is honored, and `meta.data_hash` is populated everywhere
and moves only when the data moves.

The likely mechanism is a run id derived from a second-resolution timestamp, so
two calls in the same second collide onto one id and two calls across a second
boundary produce two. Either behavior could be the intended one; they cannot
both be.
design:
Decide what a retried `replay` should do, then make it do that regardless of
timing.

If a retry should produce a fresh run, the id needs enough entropy or enough
resolution that two calls never collide. If a retry should be a no-op that
returns the existing run, that should hold across a second boundary too, which
means keying on the source run and the case set rather than on the clock.

The second reading matches how `run --run-id` already treats a completed run,
so it is probably the consistent answer.
acceptance_criteria:
- Two `replay` calls in the same wall-clock second and two calls across a second boundary produce the same outcome as each other.
- The chosen semantics are documented in `capabilities` and the CHANGELOG.
- A regression test exercises both timings explicitly, with the boundary crossing forced rather than hoped for.
- `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` continues to be honored.
- Existing report hashes are unaffected, or the change to them is stated in the CHANGELOG.
close_reason: F8: default replay id now derived from source run identity + replayed case set, not a second-resolution timestamp. A retry is idempotent (returns existing run, matching run --run-id) regardless of wall-clock second; identity mismatch still E_RUN_CONFLICT without --force; --force always rebuilds. SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH still honored for timestamps, no longer affects the id. Regression test forces same-second and cross-boundary timings via SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH. Semantics documented in replay verb description + CHANGELOG. Commit 5168214.

title: Make the unsandboxed-runner acknowledgement gate something, or remove it
description:
Closes finding F13 of the v0.4.3 make-cli conformance sweep.

`acknowledged_unsandboxed_runner` is always written `true` and gates nothing.
Proved rather than assumed: the field was hand-edited to `false` and `run`
still completed normally and `validate` still passed.

evalctl executes a runner command and a scorer command taken from a suite file
as local code, which the tool states plainly in `doctor` -- `runner_safety`
reports `sandboxed: false` and raises `W_UNSANDBOXED_RUNNER`. That honesty is
good. What is not good is shipping a field named like a gate that has never
gated anything, because a reader of the artifact reasonably concludes a safety
decision was recorded and enforced.

Read together with F22, evalctl publishes an unreachable safety-block exit code
and has no safety block, while executing arbitrary commands from a file.
design:
Two coherent options.

Make it real: refuse to run an unacknowledged suite, exit 2, and require an
explicit flag or config entry to proceed. That supplies the missing emitter for
exit 2 and makes this bead and the exit-code bead one fix.

Or remove it: delete the field, keep `W_UNSANDBOXED_RUNNER`, and state in the
docs that evalctl is not a sandbox and suites must be inspected before running.
The warning already says exactly this.

The second is defensible for a local eval harness and is less work. What is not
defensible is the current state, where the artifact records an acknowledgement
that was never sought and never checked.
acceptance_criteria:
- Either the field gates a real refusal, or it no longer exists in any artifact.
- If it gates: an unacknowledged suite refuses to run, exits 2, and the envelope names the acknowledgement flag needed to proceed. A test asserts the refusal and a second test asserts the acknowledged path runs.
- If it is removed: no artifact writes it, the docs state that evalctl does not sandbox runner or scorer commands, and `W_UNSANDBOXED_RUNNER` remains on every run envelope.
- Either way, no field in any artifact records an acknowledgement that nothing checks.
- The decision is recorded in the CHANGELOG, since it changes an artifact's shape.
close_reason:
Fixed in commits bb99770 (gate + field removal), ec71bd4 (guard test); released as 0.4.4.

All acceptance criteria met. The always-true acknowledged_unsandboxed_runner
scaffold field is removed from every artifact. run/run --resume/replay now
refuse an unacknowledged runner with E_UNSANDBOXED_RUNNER_UNACK (class safety,
exit 2) before executing any command; the acknowledgment lives with the invoker
(--acknowledge-unsandboxed-runner flag or EVALCTL_ACKNOWLEDGE_UNSANDBOXED_RUNNER=1),
not the suite file, because a suite-file field cannot defend against an untrusted
suite. W_UNSANDBOXED_RUNNER still rides every run/replay envelope. Tests assert
both the refusal and the acknowledged path (and that a suite-file field does not
satisfy the gate). Decision recorded in CHANGELOG 0.4.4 and the security docs.

title: Pin the remaining output schemas and publish the output vocabularies
description:
Closes findings F6, F18 and F24 of the v0.4.3 make-cli conformance sweep.

Three gaps in one surface, closeable in one pass.

F18. Eleven of fifteen verbs have no schema golden. `tests/goldens/` holds
`capabilities.json`, `help.txt`, `robot-docs-guide.txt`, an errors directory,
and schema goldens for `jobs`, `plan` and `run` only.

F6. `doctor`, `status`, `report` and `replay` output schemas are unpinned, so
their shapes can drift without any test noticing.

F24. No schema anywhere declares an enum, so no output vocabulary is published:

    $ evalctl schema --json | jq '.data.schemas | length'
    14
    $ evalctl schema --json | jq -c '.data.definitions'
    {}
    $ evalctl schema --json | grep -c '"enum"'
    0

Two enumerations appear in real output and neither is in the contract: run
state (`completed`, and whatever else exists) and case status, which appears as
the keys of `status_counts` -- `pass`, `fail`, `error`. The schema types
`status_counts` as an open map, so the keys are absent from it.

The cost is specific: an agent branching on case status learns the values by
observing output and can never know it has seen the full set. A suite where
nothing errors never reveals that `error` exists.
design:
Add schema goldens for the eleven unpinned verbs, using the same volatile-field
normalization the existing goldens already use -- `request_id`, `ts_iso`,
`elapsed_ms`, and `tool_version` normalized to a placeholder.

Fill the `definitions` block, which is already exported and empty, with the
case-status and run-state vocabularies, and reference them from every schema
that carries those fields. That is the smallest change that turns the
vocabularies into contract.

While in this surface, check whether any other field in the fourteen schemas is
a closed set typed as an open one.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every one of the fifteen verbs has a schema golden, and a test fails if a verb is added without one.
- `doctor`, `status`, `report` and `replay` schemas are pinned.
- `evalctl schema --json` declares the case-status vocabulary and the run-state vocabulary as enums, reachable from `definitions`.
- Every schema carrying a case status or a run state references the shared definition rather than restating it.
- A test asserts that the statuses a real run can produce are exactly the published enum, so the two cannot drift.
- Goldens normalize volatile fields the same way the existing goldens do.
close_reason: F18: schema goldens for all 14 JSON verbs, driven from DATA_SCHEMAS with a coverage test that fails on a golden-less verb. F6: doctor/status/report/replay schemas now pinned. F24: definitions publishes case_status, run_state, plan_action as enums, $ref'd from every carrier; case_status enum pinned to exactly what a real run produces; queue_jobs.state left open as a spoolctl-owned vocabulary. Commit ba40365.

title: Fake spoolctl show returns a flat job dict; real one nests it under job
description:
The fake spoolctl fixture's `show` verb emits the job record flat, with `state` and `attempts` at the top level. Real spoolctl 0.4.11 emits {job: {...}, attempts: [...], events: [...]}, where the job's own state lives at job.state and only attempts/events are top-level.

evalctl/runner.py writes per-case job.json as {job_id, state: detail.get("state") or attempt.get("state")}. Against the real binary detail.get("state") is always None, so the first branch is dead and job.json records the ATTEMPT state ("succeeded") rather than the JOB state ("done"). Against the fake the first branch wins and records the fake's flat state. Two different provenance values, and the fixture hides which one ships.

This is the same class of defect as the duration_ms bug fixed under evalctl-ede: the fake was written from evalctl's expectations rather than from spoolctl's output, so a read that never works against the real tool looks covered. The attempt key set is now asserted against both sides by REAL_SPOOLCTL_ATTEMPT_KEYS; the enclosing show envelope is not.
design:
Two parts, in order.

1. Make the fake's show envelope match real spoolctl: {job: <flat job dict>, attempts: [...], events: []}. Extend the two-sided drift check that REAL_SPOOLCTL_ATTEMPT_KEYS already performs for attempt keys so it also covers the show envelope's top-level key set. A future divergence in the wrapper then fails a test instead of being absorbed.

2. Decide and pin what job.json's `state` means. The two candidates are the job's terminal state (done, failed, canceled) and the last attempt's state (succeeded, failed, timed_out). The job state is the better provenance record -- it is what an operator sees from spoolctl -- but changing it is visible in run artifacts.

Constraint carried from evalctl-ede: tests/test_real_spoolctl.py's test_queued_run_records_queue_provenance_in_the_manifest passes today because the real path records "succeeded". Whichever value is chosen, that test must be updated deliberately as part of this issue, and the choice stated in the changelog rather than silently reconciled.
acceptance_criteria:
- The fake's show payload has the same top-level key set as real spoolctl's, asserted from one shared constant against both the fake and the real binary.
- job.json's `state` records the same value whether a run goes through the fake or the real binary, and a test asserts that.
- The chosen meaning of job.json `state` is documented, and the changelog names the change if the recorded value moves.
- The full suite passes with and without spoolctl on PATH.
close_reason: Fixed in d0c5f75. The fake's show verb now emits {job, attempts, events} like real spoolctl 0.4.11, with the job record nested and its state mapped to the real job vocabulary (done, dead, canceled). REAL_SPOOLCTL_SHOW_KEYS and REAL_SPOOLCTL_TERMINAL_JOB_STATES extend the existing two-sided drift check from the attempt record to the envelope. Decision on job.json's state field: it records the JOB state, not the last attempt's. job.json is queue provenance, so it carries spoolctl's verdict on the job; the attempt state would restate what runner.json already records, and does not exist for a job no worker ran. Recorded values move: succeeded -> done, failed and timed_out -> dead, and a canceled job records 'canceled' where it previously recorded null. Named in the changelog. job.json is not in the report projection, so report hashes are unaffected. test_queued_run_records_queue_provenance_in_the_manifest was updated deliberately from 'succeeded' to 'done' -- it had been passing on the fallback value. New tests were verified to fail against the old top-level read. Full suite green with and without spoolctl on PATH.

title: Evalctl v0.2 Authoring and Execution Replay
description:

title: Add command-scorer protocol
description:
`run_scorer` is a closed dispatch over eight deterministic built-in scorers; there is no
way to score a case with an external program. v0.2 adds a `command` scorer type — the
external scorer seam that is also the future LLM-judge seam — so a suite can score a case
by running an arbitrary program that emits a JSON verdict. Because report and replay
recompute case status from artifacts and never trust `score.json`, a non-deterministic
external scorer must be captured as an artifact, not re-executed.
design:
Add a `command` branch to `run_scorer`, and thread `case_dir: Path` and `execute: bool`
through `score_case` and `run_scorer`. `run_case` calls with `execute=True`;
`recompute_case_score` calls with `execute=False`.

Scorer config entry:
`{"name":"command","id":"<unique>","required":bool,"argv":[...]|"command":"...","shell":bool,"timeout_seconds":N}`.
The `id` is required for command scorers (a suite may have several, all named
`"command"`), must be path-safe (no separators, no `..`, no unsafe filename chars), and
names the verdict artifact.

Execute path (run time): invoke once per case with `EVALCTL_CASE_FILE` (persisted
`input.json`), `EVALCTL_OUTPUT_FILE` (persisted `output.txt`), and `EVALCTL_WORKSPACE`;
cwd is the case workspace; argv/command gets the same `$EVALCTL_*` substitution as the
runner. Persist the parsed verdict to `cases/<case_id>/scorers/<id>.json`. This artifact
is a runner-class input, captured once, never regenerated.

Replay path (report time): read the persisted verdict artifact; never execute. Deterministic
scorers keep recomputing as today.

Process hardening (mirror the runner): `subprocess.Popen(..., start_new_session=True)`
with `os.killpg` process-group kill on timeout; `timeout_seconds` from a named default
when omitted; byte-capped stdout/stderr with decode-and-replace; apply the suite's
redaction patterns and redacted env values before persisting; write capped/redacted
`cases/<case_id>/scorers/<id>.stdout.txt` and `.stderr.txt` for debugging.

Verdict normalization: stdout must parse as exactly one JSON object after trimming
whitespace (extra non-whitespace output is a scorer error); `ok` required boolean;
`score` required finite numeric constrained to 0.0..1.0 (reject NaN/Infinity and
out-of-range); `label` required string, normalized to `"pass"`/`"fail"` from `ok` when
missing/empty; `findings` required list, string entries normalized to `{"why": <string>}`.
`error:true` from a zero-exit process is a case error.

Status mapping: required scorer `ok:false,error:false` -> case `fail`; advisory scorer
`ok:false` does not fail the case; `error:true` or any normalization failure -> case
`error` regardless of `required`. A nonzero exit, timeout, or unparseable/invalid verdict
produces a scorer result carrying `error:true` and `error_code:"E_SCORER_CASE_FAILED"`,
which drives the case to `status:"error"` via the existing `s.get("error")` path — never
an orchestrator abort.

Carry the scorer `id` through every scores projection: the result object, the manifest
case entry, and the report/status failure projections — omitting the key when absent so
deterministic-only suites' `report_hash` is byte-unchanged.

Add `E_SCORER_CASE_FAILED` to the code registry (class `tool-env`, surface `score_json`
as a machine-token parallel to `runner_json`, where `["run","replay"]`); keep the
existing envelope-abort `E_SCORER_FAILED` distinct. A command-scorer is arbitrary local
code covered by the existing always-in-envelope unsandboxed-runner warning.
acceptance_criteria:
- A suite with a passing command-scorer scores the case pass and writes `cases/<id>/scorers/<id>.json`.
- Copy the run dir, delete the scorer binary, and `report --run-dir <copy>` reproduces the original `report_hash` (verdict is an artifact, never re-executed).
- Two command scorers, one passing and one failing: the report identifies the failing scorer by `id`.
- Invalid `score` type, NaN/Infinity, missing `ok`, extra stdout, and `error:true` from a zero-exit process each yield case `error`; a required scorer `ok:false,error:false` yields `fail`; an advisory scorer `ok:false` does not fail the case.
- A nonzero-exit or non-JSON scorer yields `status:"error"`, `W_PARTIAL_RUN`, run exits 0 (6 under `--fail-on-fail`), no envelope `errors[]`.
- Command-scorer timeout kills the process group; stdout/stderr are byte-capped and redacted in the persisted debug artifacts.
notes:
COMPLETED:
- Implemented command-scorer execution and report-time artifact replay.
- Added verdict normalization, per-case scorer failure handling, scorer id projection, timeout process-group kill, redacted/capped debug artifacts.
- Added CLI-surface tests for command-scorer pass/fail/error/advisory/timeout behavior.

title: Implement replay --failed execution replay
description:
Only artifact replay exists today: a copied run dir reproduces its report, but there is
no way to re-execute a failed case after fixing the runner or fixtures. `replay --failed`
re-runs only the failed/errored cases of a prior run against the current suite, into a
fresh run linked to the source, so a fix turns a red case green in a new run. `manifest.replayed_from`
is already reserved but never populated.
design:
Add `evalctl replay --failed <source-run-id|--run-dir PATH> [--suite S] [--run-id NEW] [--force] [--json]`
with its own source parser — do NOT reuse `resolve_run`, which strips only
`--run-dir`/`--format` and would misread `--failed`/`--run-id`. Exactly one source is
required (positional id XOR `--run-dir`; both or neither -> `E_CASE_INVALID`). `--run-id`
is destination-only. `--failed` is the only selector in v0.2; missing it -> `E_CASE_INVALID`.

Select failed targets from `report_data(source_run)` (the recomputed projection), NOT
from stored `manifest.cases[].status` — the manifest status is a run-time summary, while
the authoritative reportable state is recomputed from artifacts (command-scorer verdicts
included). Targets are cases whose recomputed `status != "pass"`. Use the manifest only
for provenance and id/artifact metadata.

Resolve the current suite: default to `manifest.suite.name` resolved the way `run`
resolves a suite; `--suite <suite-or-path>` overrides (needed because the manifest stores
only suite name+hash, `suite.json.name` can differ from the directory, and a copied
`--run-dir` may sit where `evals/suites/<name>` does not exist). Resolution failure ->
`E_SUITE_NOT_FOUND` with a hint to pass `--suite`. Intersect targets with the current
suite's cases; a selected case absent from the current suite is dropped with
`W_REPLAY_CASE_ABSENT`, never fabricated.

Produce a coherent PARTIAL run over exactly the re-executed cases: fresh run dir (default
run id `<source>-replay-<UTC-ts>`, `--run-id` overrides), snapshot the CURRENT suite,
re-run the selected cases through the shared executor. Factor the executor loop out of
`command_run` into a shared `execute_cases(...)` helper both call. Write the manifest with
`replayed_from = <source run_id>` and `cases[]` = the replayed subset; `manifest.suite.case_count`
is the subset count, explicitly not the full current suite count. Emit the always-in-envelope
unsandboxed-runner warning (replay re-executes runner code) and `W_PARTIAL_RUN` when any
replayed case errors.

Overwrite gating: fresh dir needs no gate. `--run-id` naming an existing completed run
requires `--force`; without it -> `E_RUN_CONFLICT` (exit 5). `--force` does not remove a
busy reservation dir (stays `E_RUN_BUSY`). Reject destination == source even under
`--force` (e.g. `--run-id r1` on source `r1`, or a `--run-dir` destination resolving to
the source path) with `E_RUN_CONFLICT` before writing anything, so replay never destroys
the source it needs.

Zero targets (all-green source) is a successful no-op: exit 0 with
`{"replayed_from":...,"cases_replayed":0}` and `W_NOTHING_TO_REPLAY`.

Add `W_REPLAY_CASE_ABSENT` and `W_NOTHING_TO_REPLAY` to the registry; add `replay` to the
`where` of `E_RUN_CONFLICT` and the unsandboxed-runner warning.
acceptance_criteria:
- A red case + a runner fix, then `replay --failed <run>`, yields a fresh run whose `manifest.replayed_from` is the source id, containing only the previously-red case, now `status:"pass"`, exit 0.
- Deleting/corrupting the source `cases/*/score.json` still lets `report <source>` name the red case AND `replay --failed` select the same case (selection from `report_data`, not the manifest summary).
- An all-green source yields `cases_replayed:0`, `W_NOTHING_TO_REPLAY`, exit 0.
- Source id both before and after replay flags resolves to the same source; `--run-dir PATH --run-id NEW` keeps source and destination distinct; missing `--failed` -> `E_CASE_INVALID`; both positional source and `--run-dir` -> `E_CASE_INVALID`.
- A suite whose `suite.json.name` differs from its directory, run by path, then replayed with `--suite <path>` after a fix, resolves and re-runs correctly.
- `--run-id` onto an existing completed run without `--force` -> `E_RUN_CONFLICT` exit 5; with `--force` overwrite succeeds; `replay --failed r1 --run-id r1 --force` -> `E_RUN_CONFLICT` exit 5 with the source manifest byte-identical.
- A selected case removed from the current suite -> `W_REPLAY_CASE_ABSENT`, skipped.
notes:
COMPLETED:
- Added replay --failed with a dedicated source parser, --suite override, projection-based failed selection, partial run manifests, zero-target no-op behavior, overwrite/source guards, and absent-case warnings.
- Factored the run executor into execute_cases shared by run and replay.
- Added CLI-surface tests for replay grammar, current-suite fixes, projection selection, overwrite guards, --suite override, and absent cases.

title: Add suite add authoring verb
description:
Suites can only be created by `init_project`, which scaffolds the fixed sample. There is
no way to create a new empty suite from the CLI, forcing hand-authored JSON. `suite add`
creates a minimal valid suite that `case add` and `scorer add` then fill.
design:
Add `evalctl suite add <name> [--runner-argv "..."] [--runner-command "..."] [--shell] [--json]`.
Create `evals/suites/<name>/` with a minimal valid `suite.json` (name,
`cases: "cases.jsonl"`, a runner block from the flags with the v0.1 defaults for
`timeout_seconds`, `max_output_bytes`, `env_allowlist`, empty redaction), an empty
`cases.jsonl`, and a `fixtures/` dir. Runner form is mutually exclusive (`--runner-argv`
XOR `--runner-command`+`--shell`), validated up front the way `validate_suite` validates
runner config.

The `<name>` is path-contained: reject path separators, `..`, empty segments, or any name
that normalizes outside `evals/suites` with `E_CASE_INVALID`.

Atomic multi-file creation: a new suite is a directory plus multiple files, so per-file
atomic writes do not prevent a half-created suite dir. If the destination already exists,
decide idempotent-match vs conflict before writing anything. Otherwise build a temporary
sibling dir under `evals/suites/`, populate it fully, run `validate_suite` on it, then
`os.replace`/rename into place only on success.

Idempotency: an existing suite dir with a byte-identical `suite.json` -> `created:false`,
return name. Existing with different content -> `E_RUN_CONFLICT` (exit 5). Never overwrite
an authored suite. An empty suite (zero cases) validates as `case_count:0, valid:true`.
acceptance_criteria:
- `suite add demo --runner-argv "python3 $EVALCTL_WORKSPACE/r.py"` creates `evals/suites/demo/{suite.json,cases.jsonl,fixtures/}`, and `validate demo` passes with `case_count:0`.
- Re-running the identical command -> `created:false`.
- The same name with a different runner -> `E_RUN_CONFLICT`, exit 5.
- A name with a path separator or `..` -> `E_CASE_INVALID`.
- A forced failure mid-creation leaves no half-built suite dir (temp-dir-and-rename).
notes:
COMPLETED:
- Added suite add with safe suite names, runner flag grammar, idempotent existing-suite detection, and temp-dir creation with validation-before-rename.
- Added CLI tests for creation, validation, idempotency, conflict, invalid names, runner grammar, and rollback via injected validation failure.

title: Add case add authoring verb
description:
Cases exist only as hand-written JSONL lines; no verb appends one. `case add` appends a
valid case to an existing suite, assigning and returning its id, so a suite can be built
entirely from the CLI.
design:
Add `evalctl case add <suite> --task "..." --workspace <path> [--id ID] [--diff <path>] [--expect-json '<json>'] [--json]`.
Append one line to `cases.jsonl` in the existing on-disk form (one `stable_json(case)`
per line, trailing newline) so unrelated cases do not churn.

Canonical construction order (this is how idempotency is judged): parse flags -> build the
body WITHOUT id -> compute the generated id if `--id` is absent (the same rule
`load_cases` uses: content-hash slice) -> set `id` -> serialize with `stable_json`. Retry
comparison is against that canonical body including the generated id, so a retry never
looks different merely because one object had an explicit id and the other did not.

`--expect-json` parses into the case's `expect` field, not a new `expect_json` field; an
absent/empty `--expect-json` omits `expect` entirely (does not write `"expect": {}`) and
retries must match that choice.

Path containment: reject absolute `--workspace`/`--diff` and any relative path containing
`..` with `E_CASE_INVALID`; store normalized POSIX-relative paths. The workspace (and diff
if given) must also exist under the suite dir, matching the validator.

Idempotency: an existing case whose canonical body matches -> `created:false`, return id.

title: validate must resolve runner argv and scorer names; --runner-argv must reject a JSON array
description:
Closes findings F16 and F15 of the v0.4.3 make-cli conformance sweep.

`validate` returns `valid: true` on a suite whose runner argv does not resolve
and whose scorer name is not a known scorer. Two of the five things its own
description claims to check are unchecked.

The cost lands on evalctl's own prescribed workflow. `robot-docs guide` step 3
tells an agent to validate before running. An agent that does gets `valid:
true`, runs, and gets one errored case at exit 0 with `ok: true`. The whole
chain was demonstrated end to end during the sweep. It compounds with the
exit-code finding: nothing in the sequence ever reports a problem.

F15 is how such a suite gets authored. `--runner-argv` accepts a JSON array and
silently coerces it into a single argument:

    suite add <name> --runner-argv '["python3","runner.py"]'

produces one argv element containing the literal bracket-and-quote text. The
suite validates. The run errors. Nothing between the two says why.
design:
`validate` should resolve what it claims to check: the runner argv's executable
against `PATH` and the workspace, and each scorer name against the registry of
known scorers. An unresolvable scorer name is the easier half -- the valid set
is small, fixed and already in the tool, so the error can carry it as
`valid_values` with a `did_you_mean`, which is the pattern the tool already
uses in `doctor --component`.

For the runner argv, an executable that does not resolve at validate time may
still resolve at run time in a different environment, so this may warrant a
warning rather than an error. A warning is fine; silence is not.

`--runner-argv` should reject a JSON array with a message naming the shape it
wants, since the flag takes a shell-style argv string. This is an input-surface
change and needs grammar tests through the real parser.
acceptance_criteria:
- `validate` on a suite with an unknown scorer name fails, names the scorer, and carries the valid scorer set in the error.
- `validate` on a suite whose runner executable does not resolve reports it, as an error or a warning, and never silently returns `valid: true`.
- The five checks named in `validate`'s description are each exercised by a test that makes the corresponding check fail.
- `--runner-argv '["a","b"]'` is rejected with a message naming the expected form, rather than coerced.
- Grammar tests cover `--runner-argv` with a JSON array, an empty string, an unbalanced quote, and a valid argv string.
- The end-to-end chain is pinned: a suite with a bad scorer ref cannot pass `validate`.
close_reason: validate now resolves scorer names against the registry (unknown -> E_CASE_INVALID + valid_values + did_you_mean, F16) and the runner executable (unresolvable -> W_RUNNER_UNRESOLVED warning, F16); --runner-argv rejects a JSON array (F15). Commit bd5c143.

title: Read the make-cli reference set and re-derive pre-flight
description:

sweep mark rows from memory of what a principle says -- the same class of

The binding rule for the whole sweep: **a checklist row may be marked only

    references/introspection.md   capabilities, schema, robot-docs, --help

    references/async.md           jobs, reservations, --wait

Read on demand, when a verb raises the question and before that row is marked:

F12 critical -- `<verb> --help` is ignored and the verb executes instead.
              `init --help` in an empty directory scaffolds evals/.
              `run <suite> --help` executes the full suite and writes a run
              directory. Only bare `evalctl --help` prints help. This is three

              the two verbs an agent probes first; per-verb --help, which is
              introspection Layer 1, does not exist; and capabilities lists
              --help in every verb's flags, so the contract states it is valid.

              settles part of z3y.4's introspection scope.

              path writes it true, including suite add --shell with no warning,
              and a suite hand-edited to false still runs to completion and
              still validates. An inert safety flag is worse than none.

              under the sample suite disappeared while the envelope listed only
              what was written. jobs prune's unconfirmed dry run is the pattern
              to copy.
F15 med   -- --runner-argv silently accepts a JSON array and stores it as one
              nonsense argument. The documented form is a shell-like string.
              An empty value is caught; a well-formed wrong value is not.
F16 med   -- validate reports valid:true for that suite. The runner argv head
              is never resolved, so the one check that would catch F15 is
              missing. F15 and F16 compound.
F17 med   -- init in an unwritable directory returns E_RUNNER_FAILED exit 3:
              wrong subsystem, exit code undeclared for init in capabilities,
              a leaked raw exception string, and a hint telling the caller to
              pass --json when they already did.
F18 low   -- extends F6: eleven of fifteen verbs have no schema golden.
F19 low   -- case add has no --from-stdin and no bulk form; authoring an
              N-case suite costs N process spawns.

E_RUN_CONFLICT on a same-id different-content add, workspace existence checked,
exact enum errors. It is the model the other three should be measured against.
