the sweep must not stop at them.

One of these leads was itself wrong on first pass, which is the reason the
rule exists: a probe looked for a top-level `mega_commands` key, found none,
and concluded evalctl advertised no mega-command mapping at all. False. The
lesson carried forward: an absent top-level key is not evidence about per-verb
data. Check the level the contract actually specifies.
design:
Lead 1 -- mega-command metadata is per-verb, with no top-level index.
Verified: `capabilities --json` reports
`data.verbs.doctor.mega_command == "DIAGNOSE"` and
`data.verbs.plan.mega_command == "PLAN"`, set in
`evalctl/static_contract.py:131` and `:146`, copied out by
`capabilities_entry_from_spec`, and already asserted in
`tests/test_evalctl.py`. The open question is narrower:

    capabilities advertises mega-command roles per verb, but not as a top-level
    mega-command index. The sweep must decide whether per-verb metadata is enough.

`references/mega-commands.md` decides it. Related and genuinely absent:
sibling spoolctl, same archetype, additionally publishes `probe_vocabularies`,
`totality`, `contract_policy`, `code_registry`, `job_states` and
`attempt_states` at the top level; evalctl publishes none of those. Whether
any is required is for the sweep to decide.

Lead 2 -- the inferctl doctor probe looks already compliant.
`probe_inferctl_component` (`evalctl/doctor.py:135`) reports
`route_available`. The standing question of whether v0.4's route capture got
doctor coverage looks like a confirm, not a gap. Say so explicitly and close
the question rather than carrying it a third time.

Lead 3 -- bounded-list coverage beyond `jobs list`. v0.4 bounded `jobs list`
only. Any other verb returning an unbounded collection owes the same
`--limit`, cursor and truncation message.

Lead 4 -- `tool_version` is pinned literally at `tests/test_evalctl.py:226`,
so a version bump edits a test. Known and deliberate; decide whether it stays
deliberate.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each of the four leads is confirmed or refuted by a pasted invocation, not
  by source reading.
- Lead 1 produces an explicit decision on whether per-verb mega-command
  metadata suffices, judged against `references/mega-commands.md`, plus a
  decision on each of the six top-level keys spoolctl publishes and evalctl
  does not.
- Lead 2 is closed explicitly, either as a confirm or as a gap -- it is not
  carried forward a third time.
- Lead 3 names every verb returning an unbounded collection.
- Lead 4 records a decision.
- No code fix is made in this bead.
notes:
All four leads resolved by invocation. Rows, evidence and one new finding are
in `evalctl-conformance-findings-2026-07-29.md`, section 'Seed observations'.
No code changed.

Lead 1 -- per-verb mega-command metadata. Confirmed present and decided
SUFFICIENT. capabilities reports verbs.doctor.mega_command DIAGNOSE and
verbs.plan.mega_command PLAN. mega-commands.md gives one instruction for a tool
with more than one mega-command: expose them as named subcommands and
cross-reference in capabilities. evalctl does exactly that. No top-level index
is specified anywhere in the reference. Not a gap.

The six top-level keys spoolctl publishes and evalctl does not, judged one by
one:
  code_registry       not a gap. evalctl has it as error_codes: 33 entries,
                      each with class, exit, surface and the verbs that raise
                      it. Different name, same content.
  totality            not a gap. Applies to one verb, jobs list, and is already
                      carried there as meta.pagination and meta.truncated.
  probe_vocabularies  not required. The DIAGNOSE shape does not ask for probe
                      names in capabilities. Noted, unnumbered: the seven
                      doctor components are learnable only by triggering
                      E_UNKNOWN_COMPONENT, which is the correct valid-set
                      pattern but a guess-wrong-to-learn path.
  contract_policy     not a gap on its own. No reference requires a
                      machine-readable policy field, and the CHANGELOG states
                      the contract position in prose every release. The
                      machine-readable half is already F21.
  job_states          real gap -> F24.
  attempt_states      real gap -> F24.

F24 med -- no output vocabulary is published anywhere in the contract. Two
           enumerations appear in real output: run state ('completed') and case
           status (the keys of status_counts: pass, fail, error). Neither is
           published. schema run types status_counts as an open map, so the
           keys are absent from it. Across the whole export: 14 schemas, 7,626
           bytes, zero occurrences of 'enum', and definitions empty. An agent
           branching on case status learns the values by observing output and
           can never know it has seen the full set -- a suite where nothing
           errors never reveals that 'error' exists. The fix is local: an enum
           on the two fields, or a definitions entry each. definitions is
           already in the export and empty, so the slot exists.

Lead 2 -- inferctl doctor probe. CONFIRMED COMPLIANT. Closed, not carried
forward again. Exercised through all four states with a stub inferctl on PATH,
the same technique evalctl's own suite uses for spoolctl: route present ->
healthy with route_available true; preflight only -> healthy with
route_available false, so the key flips rather than disappearing and an agent
can branch without a key-existence check; no preflight -> degraded; absent from
PATH -> not_configured with an all-clear. Four distinguishable states, and a
missing optional integration is not reported as a failure.

Lead 3 -- bounded lists. CONFIRMED as a gap and quantified; this is the
evidence behind F5. Exactly one verb carries --limit or --cursor: jobs.
Exactly three verbs return an unbounded per-case collection: plan, status,
report. That is the complete list. validate and run return summaries; doctor's
seven components are a fixed vocabulary, not input-scaled. plan is the one that
hurts, at ~660 bytes per case against status's ~58: on a 402-case suite, plan
returns 257,612 bytes in one envelope with pagination null, truncated null, and
--limit rejected. Noted, unnumbered: the did-you-mean for --limit offers
--timeout, a valid command with unrelated semantics.

Lead 4 -- literal tool_version pin. DECIDED: keep the intent, change the form.
Four files carry the version; one is a test, at tests/test_evalctl.py:227. The
goldens are not among them -- they normalize the field to <TOOL_VERSION>, which
is correct. So there is exactly one literal and its purpose is real: catching
the envelope's tool_version drifting from the shipped package. Recommend
assertEqual(caps['tool_version'], evalctl.__version__), which catches the same
drift and takes a test out of the set of files a release bump must touch.
Left deliberately as it is: line 226 pins the capabilities data_hash literally
and the golden carries the same hash, so a capability change re-pins twice.
Mild duplication, and it is the drift alarm schema-evolution.md asks for.
close_reason: All four leads resolved by invocation, none by source reading. Lead 1: per-verb mega-command metadata is sufficient, decided against mega-commands.md, and each of the six top-level keys spoolctl publishes was judged separately -- code_registry and totality are present under other names, probe_vocabularies and contract_policy are not required, and job_states/attempt_states are a real gap now filed as F24 (no output vocabulary is published anywhere: 14 schemas, zero enums, empty definitions). Lead 2: the inferctl doctor probe is compliant, proved through all four states with a stub binary; closed, not carried forward. Lead 3: exactly three verbs return unbounded per-case collections -- plan, status, report -- and plan returns 257 KB on a 402-case suite with --limit rejected. Lead 4: keep the tool_version drift check, replace the string literal with a comparison to the package version. Evidence in the findings document. No code fix made, per the epic's rule.

title: Write the conformance findings document
description:
No fix lands inside the conformance sweep. This bead produces findings only.
A defect found here becomes its own bead with its own acceptance criteria.

The sweep's rows are worthless unrecorded. The document is the artifact that
makes the next gate expiry measurable, and it must be written before any bead
is created from it, so prioritization happens over the whole picture rather
than verb by verb.
design:
Write `evalctl-make-cli-conformance-2026-07-XX.md` (date it on the day the
sweep completes) alongside the roadmap, containing:

- one row per verb per checklist item -- met / not met / not applicable -- each
  "met" row carrying the invocation that proves it and the reference file it
  was judged against;
- the before-ship list under the same rule, including the determinism check as
  it was run;
- a findings list ranked by archetype weight, each finding naming the
  checklist item, the observed behavior, and a proposed bead;
- explicit statement of every row deliberately marked not applicable, with the
  reason. The previous checklist's failure was a silent wrong "met", and a
  silent "n/a" is the same failure wearing a different hat.
acceptance_criteria:
- The document exists, is dated, and is committed alongside the roadmap.
- Every verb from all three sweeps appears, none skipped.
- Every "met" row carries both an invocation and a reference citation.
- Every "not applicable" row carries its reason.
- The findings list is ranked by archetype weight and each entry proposes a
  bead.
- No bead has been created from the findings yet -- that comes after this
  document is complete.
notes:
Document complete: `evalctl-conformance-findings-2026-07-29.md`, 1,958 lines,
stored alongside the roadmap. Structure: Method, Pre-flight, Per-verb findings
(three tranches), Quick reference, Before-ship checklist, Seed observations,
Ranked findings and proposed beads, plus three evidence appendices carrying 43
numbered exhibits.

Acceptance, item by item:

Exists and is dated -- yes, dated on the day the sweep completed.

Every verb from all three sweeps appears -- yes, all fifteen. 192 checklist-row
markings: the 12-row legend plus 180 per-verb rows, 12 rows x 15 verbs.

Every met row carries an invocation and a reference citation -- yes. This was
the binding rule for the whole sweep and no row was marked from source reading.
The one row that could not be judged from output alone, R11's 'pinned by a
regression test', was satisfied by running the test rather than reading it.

Every not-applicable row states its reason -- yes. R7, R8, R9, R10 and R12 are
the usual n/a rows and each carries its reason inline.

Findings ranked by archetype weight, each proposing a bead -- yes, new section
'Ranked findings and proposed beads'. All 24 findings ranked against sketch 5,
the build/task orchestrator, which weights PLAN, async with checkpointing,
determinism and detailed exit codes highest, DIAGNOSE high, and feedback,
TRIAGE and streaming low. Where severity and weight disagree, weight wins: F10
is a DIAGNOSE divergence on a high-weight axis but cosmetic, so it ranks 19th;
F19 is real but on a low-weight axis, so it ranks last. Each row names its
checklist item, its weight axis and its proposed bead.

Fourteen beads proposed for 24 findings. Five of them group findings that share
one fix:
  A  global flags per-verb aware      F12, F23, and B3's per-verb half   P0
  B  exit-code contract               F2, F22, and evalctl-1cx           P1
  C  in-flight runs visible           F1                                 P1
  D  unsandboxed-runner gate          F13, supplies B's exit-2 emitter   P1

No bead has been created from the findings. That is the acceptance criterion

Two deviations from the design, both cosmetic and recorded rather than hidden.

title: Create beads from the conformance findings and record the sweep
description:
No fix lands inside the conformance sweep. This bead produces findings only.
A defect found here becomes its own bead with its own acceptance criteria.

A findings document with no tracker entries decays into a document nobody
implements from. Beads are created here, after the whole picture exists, so
prioritization spans all fifteen verbs rather than happening verb by verb.

The pressure this ordering resists is real and predictable: most conformance
findings will be two-line fixes, and fixing one while it is in front of you is
faster than writing it up. That is precisely how an audit turns into an
unreviewed refactor, and how the resulting record stops describing any surface
that ever existed.

The roadmap also needs the sweep's date and outcome recorded, because the
standing guardrail -- a passed conformance gate expires when the surface it
covered changes -- is only measurable against a recorded date.
design:
For each finding, create a bead with its own acceptance criteria, priority set
from the archetype weight recorded in the findings document. Fixes are scoped
and released separately from the sweep; none of them lands in this epic.

Then edit the roadmap to record the sweep's completion date and outcome.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every finding in the document has a corresponding bead with its own
  acceptance criteria.
- No bead created here bundles a fix with the audit.
- The roadmap records the sweep's date and outcome.
- The epic can be closed: no finding is left tracked only in the document.
notes:
Fourteen beads created, covering all twenty-four findings. Each carries its own
description, design and acceptance criteria, and each is linked to the sweep
epic by a `discovered-from` dependency.

  P0  evalctl-per-verb-flags-ju1                F12, F23
  P1  evalctl-exit-code-contract-yxb            F2, F22
  P1  evalctl-inflight-run-visibility-8al       F1
  P1  evalctl-runner-safety-gate-ikb            F13
  P2  evalctl-plan-external-blockers-kxd        F3
  P2  evalctl-bounded-collections-trf           F5, F4
  P2  evalctl-validate-actually-validates-x3v   F16, F15
  P2  evalctl-error-valid-sets-o89              F7, F17, F20
  P2  evalctl-schema-pins-and-vocabulary-xg4    F6, F18, F24
  P2  evalctl-replay-clock-idempotency-s5b      F8
  P3  evalctl-diagnose-and-feedback-shape-58y   F10, F11, F9
  P3  evalctl-contract-version-type-yw7         F21
  P3  evalctl-case-add-bulk-yrz                 F19
  P3  evalctl-init-force-reporting-1lk          F14

Fourteen rather than twenty-four because in five places one fix closes several
findings and splitting them would mean touching the same code three times. The
clearest case is the error-valid-sets bead: F7, F17 and F20 are the same
omission at three different sites, and the tool already implements the correct
pattern twice elsewhere.

Priorities come from archetype weight, not severity alone. The P0 is the only
critical finding. The three P1s are the two highest-weighted axes for a
build/task orchestrator -- exit codes and async work with checkpointing -- plus
the safety gate that supplies the missing emitter for exit 2.

No bead bundles a fix with the audit. Every one is a fix bead with acceptance
criteria and no code behind it, and none is a child of the sweep epic, so the
epic can close without waiting on them.

Beads B and D also carry a `related` link to evalctl-1cx, the standing doctor
exit-code question. That bead was updated rather than closed: it stays open
because the doctor half is a real judgement call, and its notes now point at
the exit-code bead and say the two should be decided together.

Roadmap updated. The standing-rule section now records the sweep date
(2026-07-29), the version (v0.4.3), the outcome (not passed, 24 findings), the
critical finding stated in full rather than left in the document, the two
results worth carrying forward as gate history -- determinism is now the
strongest axis after capabilities, and the two questions carried by the last
two reviews are closed -- and the note that this gate expires the moment any of
the fourteen beads lands.
close_reason: Created fourteen beads covering all twenty-four findings, each with its own description, design and acceptance criteria, each linked to the sweep by discovered-from, and none a child of the epic so that the epic can close independently. Grouping is fourteen rather than twenty-four because five beads close findings that share one fix. Priorities set from archetype weight rather than severity: one P0 (the critical global-flag defect), three P1s on the two highest-weighted axes plus the safety gate, six P2s, four P3s. No bead bundles a fix with the audit. evalctl-1cx updated with a pointer to the exit-code bead and left open as a genuine decision. Roadmap's standing-rule section now records the sweep date, version, outcome, the critical finding in full, the two questions now closed, and that the gate expires when any of the fourteen beads lands.

title: Fix Fake Spoolctl Fixture Races
description:
Roadmap section 4.1. CI run 30072965277 failed on the Python 3.13 matrix job in test_queue_spoolctl_outcome_mapping_and_stdin_wrapper with a JSONDecodeError. Root cause is the fake spoolctl fixture, not any real spoolctl integration path.

In evalctl/tests/fakes.py the generated fake binary does an unguarded read-modify-write against a single shared .spoolctl.db: save() (fakes.py:46) is a plain write_text, load() (fakes.py:41) re-reads the whole file. Under --jobs, evalctl invokes the fake once per case concurrently, exposing three races:

1. Torn read - a reader observes a partially written file. This is the observed JSONDecodeError. Fixed by atomic rename.
2. Lost update - two add processes both load, both mutate, both save; the second clobbers the first job entry. NOT fixed by atomic rename.
3. Colliding job ids - job_id = "job-" + str(len(data["jobs"]) + 1) (fakes.py:82) derives the id from a snapshot both processes read before either wrote, so two cases can receive the same job-N. NOT fixed by atomic rename.

An atomic write alone is insufficient. Races 2 and 3 need a lock held across the entire read-modify-write (O_EXCL lockfile or fcntl.flock), with the atomic rename on top. Shipping only the atomic write leaves the fixture flaking intermittently rather than reliably, which is worse for a fixture because it reads as a real regression.

Acceptance:
- Fake .spoolctl.db writes use a same-directory temp file plus os.replace.
- The full load-mutate-save sequence in the fake add and work paths is serialized under a lock so concurrent fake processes cannot lose an update.
- Job-id assignment is unique under concurrency and not derived from a possibly-stale len(data["jobs"]).
- The fix does not expand the fake fixture ownership of real queue semantics. It stays a contract-shape and synthetic-failure fixture; real queue semantics coverage is roadmap 4.2.
- The Python 3.13 failing test path is covered locally or in CI.
- Ordinary local unit-test discovery still passes with no real spoolctl installed.

Out of scope: pinned real-spoolctl CI coverage (roadmap 4.2), spoolctl 0.4.2 failure_reason adoption.
close_reason: Atomic .spoolctl.db writes plus flock and counter-based job ids; regression test added
